Exit is now the weak pillar: much of the on-chain liquidity is shallow, and modest effective depth relative to headline TVL means unwinding through the basket beats trusting the order books. The early-days chaos, with dozens of brief sub-50-bps blips and one absurd upward spike near +5,000 bps, pointed to thin two-sided liquidity rather than backing failure, and that diagnosis still holds. Structurally, HONEY's basket mint and Basket Mode work like a multi-asset {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}, with permissionless atomic {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} into its underlying stablecoin reserves. It is a sound mechanism still wearing some of its host chain's risks.

wusd-worldwide.title: The Exit Toll
wusd-worldwide.text:
A dollar token that lost every venue it traded on, then charged a hundred of itself to leave the one still standing.

WSPN's Worldwide USD shed roughly 94% of its circulating supply between 2026-07-21 and mid-August: 9.99M down to 0.61M, with two burns on 07-29 and 08-01 doing most of the work. No issuer statement has accompanied the contraction. The centralized exits closed in the same window: MEXC delisted on 07-25, Bitget dropped WUSD/USDT on 07-31, and Coins.ph, the flagship retail pair, left on 08-04 with the tidy explanation that WUSD was "no longer able to adhere to our listing standards." What remains is a single Viction pool quoting around $0.95 whose ~$96k headline reserve absorbs roughly $490 before it moves 2%, which is why Pharos now publishes no price at all rather than a number nothing trades at. Direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} still functions, but only through corporate accounts that qualified businesses must apply and be verified for. A holder without a WSPN relationship is routed to a secondary market that no longer exists. The detail worth pausing on sits on Viction, where the VRC25 deployment levies a flat 100 WUSD on token calls: amount-independent, verified on-chain, and charged on approve() as well as transfer(), meaning a wallet must hold $100 of a dollar token before it can authorise a swap of any size. The F grade was already on file before any of this happened; the reserve brochure was never the binding constraint.

sources.label: Bitget: notice of delisting 6 spot trading pairs, 2026-07-31
Viction VRC25 issuer registry entry for WUSD (100 WUSD fee)

frxusd-frax.title: Frax's Clean Slate
frxusd-frax.text: frxUSD is Frax's tokenized-{{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}}-backed dollar minted and redeemed 1:1 through governance-approved custodians, a {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} do-over without legacy FRAX's algorithmic baggage. The balance sheet is narrower than the custodian roster suggests: WisdomTree's WTGXX government money-market fund is the largest holding, Superstate USTB and BlackRock BUIDL sit behind it, and a small Bridge USDB position plus a segregated bank account round it out, while the enshrined-custodian design gives users a direct exit whenever the relevant collateral is available. Governance has approved more custodians than the reserve actually uses: Superstate USCC, Agora AUSD, and Centrifuge JTRSY each cleared a FIP without ever carrying a balance, a useful reminder that an approval is a permission, not a position. The sfrxUSD wrapper passes through reserve yield, which is modestly useful and mercifully not the whole pitch. The real trade-off is concentration in a small club of tokenized-money issuers, plus Frax DAO's power to approve who holds the money and to revoke that approval. It is institutional infrastructure arranged by a crypto protocol: much tidier than old FRAX, but not magically free of gatekeepers.

usyc-hashnote.title: Circle USYC Goes Multichain
usyc-hashnote.text: USYC is Hashnote's tokenized short-duration fund share now wearing Circle's distribution jacket. The reserve mix is the clean TradFi part: mostly U.S. Treasury bills with reverse repo agreements, redeemable at NAV rather than pretending every token is a static dollar bill. That NAV behavior matters because USYC is yield-bearing fund exposure, not a payment stablecoin, and Pharos treats the issuer controls accordingly. Circle's rebrand and multichain push make the wrapper easier to move around, but the legal and operational substance remains fund administration, eligible access, and issuer-operated minting. It is a very respectable money-market instrument cosplaying just enough as crypto to become collateral elsewhere.

eurr-stablr.title: Hacked, Frozen, Compliant
eurr-stablr.text: EURR was StablR's Malta-MFSA MiCA euro e-money token, with Grant Thornton {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, Tether's strategic backing, and the full compliance stack, until a May 24, 2026 cybersecurity incident ended the experiment mid-stride. An attacker compromised StablR's minting infrastructure and printed 4.5 million unbacked EURR alongside its dollar sibling USDR; minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} were frozen, and StablR disclosed that circulating supply was no longer fully backed at the 1:1 ratio MiCAR requires. Pharos no longer scores it at all; EURR sits in the archive as a frozen incident asset, because a report card presumes a functioning redemption promise and this one has been suspended since May. StablR's recovery-plan updates through June announced forensics and specialists, not restored minting, redemption, or full backing, so the token trades, where it trades at all, on hope of recovery rather than on a claim. The Tether connection that once framed the institutional-trust question now reads differently: distribution muscle is worthless when the mint key is the thing that broke. Whether Malta's MFSA carries the weight of France's ACPR in the MiCA hierarchy is being answered in an enforcement file, not a marketing deck.

usdr-stablr.title: One Key From Compliant
usdr-stablr.text: StablR's USDR holds a Malta MFSA EMI license under MiCA with 100% reserves in cash and short-term government bonds, reviewed quarterly by Grant Thornton. The regulatory stack includes formal {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} that checks every European compliance box while the market barely notices at single-digit-millions in supply. Then May 2026 rewrote the story: an attacker compromised StablR's 1-of-3 minting multisig and printed $13.5 million of unbacked USDR and EURR, the quote broke violently below par, and the issuer froze minting and redemption while disclosing to Malta's MFSA that circulating supply was no longer fully 1:1 backed. That violated MiCA's cardinal requirement, and it happened to a MiCA poster child. Weeks later the report card reads F with the primary market still suspended, and the thin single-pool Ethereum footprint that once merely embarrassed the liquidity score now defines the only exit anyone has. With liquidity that shallow, any meaningful exit runs through StablR's own issuer API {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route rather than the order book. Europe's MiCA framework was supposed to be the catalyst for regulated stablecoins; USDR is now the test of what the framework does after the incident report is filed.

usdo-openeden.title: Treasury Yield, Repackaged
usdo-openeden.text: OpenEden's USDO is a rebasing dollar that distributes tokenized {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} yield by growing holder balances daily, backed mostly by OpenEden's own TBILL token with BUIDL, VBILL, and a thin stablecoin buffer beneath it. The trust chain is considerably longer than the $1 label implies. It moves from F to C- this release on one finding: the Bermuda Monetary Authority's regulated-entities register was read directly and upholds OpenEden Digital's Class F digital-asset licence, so prudential supervision is evidenced rather than asserted. Be clear about what the rest of that upgrade rests on. Reconciliation is graded periodic, not continuous. No issuer artefact names a reconciliation series, the Chainlink feed that does exist covers only the Treasury sleeve and diverges from the issuer's own full-basket figure by roughly nine percent, and the documentation's transparency page has been future-tense about a public dashboard for more than half a year. Pharos's own proof-of-reserves record grades that identical endpoint as self-verification with partial liability coverage, which makes this the thinnest evidence supporting a passing grade anywhere in its class; it is queued for re-verification, and the grade should be read as provisional. The rebasing design also stays awkward for anything that cannot handle a moving balance, which is precisely why cUSDO exists.

usda-anzens.title: Proof by Medium Post
usda-anzens.text: Anzens USDA claims the cleanest backing on Cardano: USD cash and {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}-managed by BitGo Trust under a FinCEN MSB registration. It nevertheless carries one of the worst peg records Pharos tracks, with hundreds of recorded depeg events against a single thin DEX pool. The problem starts with the chain and ends with the paperwork: Cardano-only deployment leaves no arbitrage infrastructure to enforce the peg, the exit pillar fails outright, and the backing pillar cannot compensate because no current reserve composition is on file to score. This release makes the paperwork worse. An evidence review pulled the reconciliation credit entirely. The proof-of-reserves 'series' turns out to be four image-only Medium posts in sixteen months, the newest covering a period now half a year stale while supply fell by roughly sixty percent, with no readable signing firm, period, or opinion, and no transparency surface on the issuer's own site. A stalled, unverifiable series cannot support recurring-reconciliation credit, so the mint posture drops to the floor and USDA sinks further inside its F rather than out of it. Sound reserves are necessary but nowhere near sufficient. The system also needs a market that can trade the thing and an issuer willing to publish a document somebody can actually read.

usdf-falcon.title: The Altcoin Basis Trade
usdf-falcon.text: Falcon Finance takes the {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} playbook and cranks the risk dial: BTC shorts, stablecoins, ETH shorts, tokenized Treasuries, and the part that separates it from Ethena: altcoins like DOGE, FET, TRX, and TON hedged with {{term:perpetual}}perp{{/term}} shorts on centralized exchanges. The live safety profile has softened, and the culprit is plain: the peg mostly behaves, but liquidity is the soft spot and the whitelisted on-chain {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path is a bottleneck. The sUSDf yield attracts capital faster than the exotic, altcoin-heavy collateral mix can comfortably support, which is exactly the tension the report card keeps pricing in. Real-time reserve transparency via ht.digital is a genuine differentiator, not a marketing footnote. But a track record of brief sub-peg blips suggests the altcoin hedging strategy stumbles where BTC-only approaches would not. USDf is Ethena's wilder cousin, and the family resemblance is not the risky part.

europ-schuman.title: Credentials Without Scale
europ-schuman.text: EUROP is Schuman Financial's ACPR-licensed euro stablecoin backed by euro cash at EU banks, with credentials in abundance despite negligible market share. Schuman stacks every credential the euro stablecoin market demands; ACPR EMI license under MiCA, quarterly KPMG reserve {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, 98% of reserves in euro cash at Société Générale and peer EU banks, a 2% buffer beyond par, yet it still circulates a float roughly the size of a mid-tier DeFi protocol's {{term:treasury}}treasury{{/term}}. The report card now reads mid-table rather than second-tier-with-an-asterisk: a C+ overall where backing earns a B- but exit liquidity and economic control both hover in C territory: the sober arithmetic of a token whose paperwork cannot conjure market depth or dilute issuer control. The peg itself is not the worry: it holds A-grade tightness and sits at the calm end of the stress scale, with dozens of brief sub-par blips that read as thin-market noise rather than structural instability. The July MiCA cutover thinned the field to a handful of authorized euro stablecoins, and EUROP's distribution bet spans XRPL, Plasma, and Solana alongside the usual EVM chains. It reaches where established euro rivals have not planted flags. But distribution without depth just spreads the same thin float across more order books.

brz-transfero.title: Pegged to Volatility Itself
brz-transfero.text: BRZ is Transfero's centralized Brazilian real stablecoin, redeemable 1:1 by KYC'd users against BRL cash held in regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at a Brazilian institution; its depeg history is FX volatility, not reserve failure. The dozens of recorded depeg events, including swings approaching 10,000 basis points below peg, are not evidence of product failure but of what happens when you peg a token to the Brazilian real and price it against dollar-denominated markets. The F safety grade follows from that FX-driven peg record once the v9 peg multiplier gets involved. The backing pillar cannot rescue the score because Pharos scores current reserve evidence rather than issuer claims, and BRZ's reserve composition simply isn't on file. The exit story has improved from the basement but remains the standing constraint: a 1% {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} fee through Transfero's offchain issuer path still means the cleanest way out of any sizable position is the issuer window, not the secondary market. Deployed across multiple chains with hundreds of millions of reais in circulation, BRZ serves a genuine need in Latin America's largest crypto market, and while it tends to sit at the calm end of the stress scale day to day, thin liquidity and the underlying FX exposure are a standing reminder that non-USD stablecoins carry risks no reserve structure can hedge away.

rlusd-ripple.title: The Institutional On-Ramp
rlusd-ripple.text: Ripple's NYDFS-supervised dollar is backed by a very-low-risk reserve split across {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, government {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market funds{{/term}}, and cash, with monthly {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} from Deloitte under a New York trust charter. That reserve is the kind of boring institutional machinery a settlement token should have, and RLUSD is very much a settlement token rather than a DeFi primitive. The live grade has eased from the earlier headline because secondary-market depth and concentration still matter even when the collateral is immaculate. Brief depeg events from early price discovery are less a reserve indictment than a reminder that new tokens need time to build market plumbing. DEX liquidity remains concentrated in a handful of pools, consistent with a payments corridor product whose real exit is issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. The paperwork keeps compounding: RLUSD launched in Japan as the first stablecoin approved under the Type 4 electronic-payment-instrument regime via SBI, Ripple's Luxembourg entity upgraded to a full MiCA CASP authorization covering the EEA, and Mastercard added RLUSD to its stablecoin settlement stack. RLUSD looks sturdy, but it is sturdy in the way a bank product is sturdy: excellent paperwork, narrow on-chain spontaneity.

feusd-felix.title: Liquity Fork on Hyperliquid
feusd-felix.text: feUSD is a Liquity-v2-fork {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} dollar on Hyperliquid, {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} by HYPE ecosystem tokens: concentrated chain risk, sturdy redemption mechanics. Felix Protocol cloned Liquity V2 onto Hyperliquid's unproven L1 and loaded the CDPs with HYPE and its liquid-staking derivatives, an asset class Pharos rates very-high risk, alongside bridged Bitcoin. The v9 report card renders a cleaner verdict than any blended score could: backing earns a B+ and the exit pillar an A, thanks to zero-fee atomic collateral {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and an interest-rate-sorted queue, yet the overall grade sits at D because economic control fails outright: a multisig still holds the admin keys, caps, and pause, and v9 treats that kind of mint authority as a first-class risk rather than a footnote. The peg itself has held tight, rarely drifting from the calm end of the stress scale despite a long tail of brief blips. The structural caveat remains: when your primary collateral is the native token of the chain you live on, a single ecosystem shock hits both your backing and your exit {{term:liquidation}}liquidity simultaneously{{/term}}: good pillar grades measure the machinery, not the correlation.

dusd-standx.title: The Quiet Basis Trader
dusd-standx.text: DUSD is StandX's {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar: an Ethena-style {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} through Ceffu {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, with less theater and less public verification. The reserve model is mostly spot-long and {{term:perpetual}}perp-short{{/term}} exposure on BTC, ETH, SOL, and BNB, plus a small stability buffer, so the product lives or dies by CEX operations and hedging discipline. The live grade remains weak because exotic collateral, centralized custody, no published proof of reserves, and an issuer-API {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path are not small footnotes. The peg record has looked cleaner than the structure deserves, which suggests the desk knows what it is doing as long as the infrastructure beneath it behaves. The stress panel has moved out of the sleepy framing the old summary used, so the right read is not panic but active monitoring. Trusting a basis trader is one thing; verifying the basis trader is the part StandX still leaves mostly off-chain.

eurcv-societe-generale-forge.title: SocGen’s Blockchain Experiment
eurcv-societe-generale-forge.text: EURCV is SG-FORGE's MiCA EUR stablecoin, with reserves held in EUR cash at SocGen itself and institutional custody constrained by the concentration cap. EUR CoinVertible is issued by SG-FORGE, the digital asset arm of a systemically important European bank, with reserves held 100% in euro cash at Société Générale. That institutional-grade {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} earns a solid B on the backing pillar while the exit pillar now grades at the very top of the scale. The {{grade}} overall grade is a story about concentration rather than quality: the score sits under a binding critical-dependency cap because reviewed reserve paths share a single upgrade-control key: v9's way of saying that one Ethereum contract admin stands between EURCV and its collateral. The DEWS stress reading is among the lowest on the entire dashboard, suggesting an operational serenity most euro stablecoins cannot claim. Deployed across Ethereum, XRPL, Stellar, and Solana with MiCA EMI licensing from France's ACPR, whether EURCV is the future of tokenized money or a corporate innovation lab's pet project depends on whether SocGen commits distribution resources that match its regulatory credentials. Direct 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through SG-FORGE.

yusd-aegis.title: Live Proof, Issuer-Controlled Exit
yusd-aegis.text:
A delta-neutral BTC-collateralized synthetic dollar with best-in-class proof-of-reserves and a failing overall grade. It offers transparency you can watch live, wrapped around exits you may not get.

Aegis YUSD is a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} stablecoin built entirely on BTC. It holds spot long at Fireblocks, Copper, and Ceffu under institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, hedged by COIN-M {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} shorts. The design is still marketed exactly as launched. The overall grade has collapsed to an F, and not because the peg misbehaves day to day: peg scoring is strong and stress signals sit at the calm end of the scale, but the exit pillar bottoms out and economic control grades at the floor. The dollar holds until you need to leave through a door the issuer controls. More than two dozen recorded depeg events with a worst excursion north of 1,700 bps tell the story of a token whose price is a function of {{term:funding-rate}}funding-rate{{/term}} economics and exchange availability, not reserve quality. Real-time proof-of-reserves through Accountable remains genuinely best-in-class transparency. You can watch the positions live, which is more than Ethena offers. Transparency does not reduce CEX custody concentration or conjure an open exit route. A {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} you can audit in real time is still a basis trade.

reusd-resupply.title: Leverage All the Way Down
reusd-resupply.text:
A CDP coin minted against Curve Lend and Fraxlend vault shares. The design wraps recursive yield in a token with a 1% redemption-fee floor.

Resupply's reUSD wraps Curve Lend and Fraxlend vault shares into a dollar token whose collateral is itself earning yield on other stablecoins. The design layers leverage atop a 1% {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} fee floor sourced from a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} architecture. The report card has slid into D territory overall, with the exit pillar the weakest of the three, and hundreds of recorded depeg events tell the tale of exotic collateral doing exotic things even as supply holds in the tens of millions. DEX liquidity remains thin and concentrated relative to that supply, so any serious exit leans on the communal redemption floor rather than the order book. The June 2025 oracle-manipulation exploit created roughly $9.6M of bad debt, which was repaid through treasury funds, insurance-pool burns, and a Yearn DAO loan. This is the footnote explaining why the vault plumbing earns skepticism. reUSD tends to camp in the watch end of the stress scale rather than the calm one, and the market prices it accordingly as a recursive instrument rather than a stable store of value. The design suits farming rather than parking.

tbill-openeden.title: T-Bills With a Token Wrapper
tbill-openeden.text: OpenEden's TBILL is a tokenized BVI professional fund holding short-dated {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills managed by BNY Investment Management under BNY custody, KYC-gated and drifting steadily above its original dollar as NAV accrues to holders rather than resetting to par. The structure functions as intended: professional investors collect on-chain Treasury yield through issuer-side mint and redemption at NAV, and everyone else can look but not touch. The paperwork is thinner than the institutional nameplates suggest. Daily NAV figures come from fund administrator Protege Fund Services, the annual auditor has published no report, and the only named controls work is a one-off Ernst & Young procedures review rather than a recurring {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. The gating has now reached its logical conclusion: since mid-July Pharos has held TBILL in quarantine because permitted market-data sources report no positive circulating supply, so the token currently carries no report card at all. The NAV oracle keeps ticking upward while the supply side of the ledger is simply invisible. A token with no DEX pools and no permissionless mint has limited market exposure, and that same construction makes TBILL unmeasurable. TBILL has become so private that even the public data can't find it.

a7a5-old-vector.title: The Sanctioned Dollar's Mirror
a7a5-old-vector.text: A7A5 is Old Vector LLC's centralized ruble stablecoin, issued under a Kyrgyz VASP license and built on deposits at sanctioned Russian state bank Promsvyazbank, though issuer materials now describe the backing only as an undisclosed basket of ruble deposits and short-term assets, and no reserve artefact has ever been published. The architecture is technically compliant at home while functionally untouchable by Western financial infrastructure, and since February 2026 the issuer has passed nearly all reserve income to holders as additional A7A5 at the CBR key rate minus one percentage point, making it one of the few {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} stablecoins whose holders directly capture a sanctioned banking system's deposit rate. The net keeps tightening: the EU's 21st sanctions package, adopted in July 2026, stopped sanctioning around the edges and designated the A7 payments network itself: A7 Agent, A71, and its African affiliates, alongside some fifteen crypto platforms including HTX, with the measures biting from late August. The market has gone quiet: after the Grinex shutdown, and with analytics firms attributing a large share of historical volume to wash trading, visible secondary trading has all but evaporated: the USD price print still tracks the ruble mostly because A7A5 never had real on-chain price discovery, which is also why headlines about a collapse to zero misread a token whose {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} loop runs entirely through KYC'd off-chain partners. Whether A7A5 represents financial innovation for an isolated economy or sanctions evasion with a token wrapper depends entirely on whose compliance framework you're applying.

sources.label: CoinGeek: EU 21st sanctions package designates A7 network and HTX (adopted 2026-07-23)

usd1-world-liberty-financial.title: World Liberty Financial Dollar
usd1-world-liberty-financial.text: World Liberty Financial's USD1 is politically loud and structurally boring, which is exactly the joke. Under the Trump-affiliated wrapper sits a BitGo Trust-issued dollar backed by short-term Treasuries, government money-market funds, and cash deposits under a South Dakota trust charter with recurring attestations. The product risk comes from centralized issuer control, role-gated minting, issuer-only redemption, and uncertainty over whether the brand helps distribution or narrows the buyer pool to people already nodding. Pharos therefore reads USD1 as a conventional regulated stablecoin wearing a campaign hat, not a new monetary primitive. The reserves are the least dramatic part, which may be the most damning thing one can say about the launch.

usdx-hex-trust.title: Claimed Treasuries, Zero-Score Exit
usdx-hex-trust.text: Hex Trust's USDX advertises T-bill and cash reserves at global tier-1 banks under a Hong Kong TCSP license, which makes its F safety grade a case study in how clean-sounding reserves mean nothing without functional market infrastructure. Supply sits across three chains (Ethereum, Flare, Songbird), but the exit pillar scores a literal zero. A single DEX pool with a few hundred dollars in effective TVL is not a liquidity profile; it's a rounding error. Hundreds of recorded depeg events and a worst deviation past 7,000 basis points tell the story of a stablecoin that periodically trades around 28 cents on the dollar despite claiming Treasuries at par. Claiming is the operative word, since no current reserve composition is on file for the backing pillar to score. The stress engine reads USDX as sitting at the calm end of the scale, but that placidity is itself the tell: there is no two-sided market thrashing the price back, so nothing registers as stress. {{term:attestation}}Attestation{{/term}} from a Hong Kong TCSP-licensed {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} provider and 270+ institutional clients haven't translated into the on-chain arbitrage loops that keep prices honest, and same-day issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} cannot substitute for the missing secondary market. This leaves USDX as expensive proof that custodial credibility and stablecoin stability are entirely different problems.

pusd-plume.title: USDC With a Detour
pusd-plume.text:
A USDC wrapper that routes through a Nucleus BoringVault with OFAC checks: extra trust layers on top of an asset that was already perfectly functional.

Plume's pUSD takes USDC, routes it through a Nucleus BoringVault with OFAC compliance checks, and issues a wrapped token on Ethereum and Plume Chain, adding smart contract risk, {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} abstraction, and a new trust layer to an asset that was already perfectly functional. The report card has crawled back into C territory as exit liquidity recovered from outright failing to merely thin. Zero-fee same-day {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} suggests the wrapper functions, but the deviation history records a dozen-plus blips capped by a catastrophic 4,049-basis-point negative excursion. The wrapper emphatically failed at least once. Supply idles in the single-digit millions with on-chain depth to match, raising the question of whether the RWAfi ecosystem narrative generates enough demand to justify the wrapper's existence. pUSD remains a solution in search of a problem that Plume hasn't yet proven it has.

bold-liquity.title: Immutable Code, Almost Perfect
bold-liquity.text: BOLD is Liquity V2's decentralized dollar stablecoin, minted from immutable {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} vaults against WETH, wstETH, and rETH only: no governance keys, no admin functions, no RWA exposure. The report card shows what that discipline buys: A+ pillars for both exit and economic control, with permissionless atomic collateral {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at 50 bps providing one of DeFi's hardest peg floors, while user-set interest rates and Stability Pool yield create self-correcting incentives that keep BOLD close to par. The one concession is a backing pillar a notch below the rest: the volatility premium for holding ETH and its staking derivatives instead of T-bills, which is precisely the trade Liquity's users signed up for. Supply keeps spreading across a widening multichain footprint, but the total remains small relative to the design's ambition, proof that the market still prices convenience and composability above architectural purity.

avusd-avant.title: Redeemable Receipt, Leveraged Book
avusd-avant.text: avUSD is Avant's centralized dollar stablecoin, redeemable 1:1 for USDC and deployed into actively managed {{term:delta-neutral}}market-neutral{{/term}} strategies for yield: avUSD itself does not accrue yield, the staked savUSD does. USDC is the mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rail rather than the reserve itself: deposited capital is routed into a leveraged market-neutral book spanning basis trades, lending arbitrage, and private liquidity deals, with the avUSDx junior tranche and a separate reserve fund absorbing strategy losses first, which is why backing sits as the weakest pillar on an otherwise middling report card. Users stake avUSD into the separately tracked savUSD senior tranche when they want yield exposure, while avUSD remains the redeemable receipt for USDC exits at a 5-basis-point fee and a one-to-seven-day settlement window. The institutional-unregulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and BVI domicile mean trust runs through Avant's operational integrity rather than a regulatory framework, which is why the backstop redemption remains queue-based rather than a hard on-chain par floor. A string of recorded depegs, including a worst reading of 321 basis points below peg, shows the market can still stress the wrapper even when the current peg score is high.

ylds-figure.title: The SEC-Registered Yield Coin
ylds-figure.text:
The only stablecoin registered under the 1933 and 1940 Acts. It pays SOFR-minus-35bps via a face-amount certificate, with full KYC and restricted transferability as the price of legitimacy.

YLDS is that rarest of crypto products: a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing stablecoin{{/term}} registered under the Securities Act of 1933 and the Investment Company Act of 1940. It pays SOFR minus 35 basis points through a fixed face-amount certificate structure that the SEC has explicitly blessed. The reserves comprise short-dated {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}}, overnight Treasury repo, and government {{term:money-market-fund}}money market funds{{/term}}. KPMG audits the qualified assets on deposit at UMB and Flagstar. They form a {{term:rwa}}real-world-asset{{/term}} stack so conservative it makes Circle look adventurous. What launched on Provenance and Solana has since spread to Ethereum and, most recently, Stellar. The deployment targets LATAM fintech and neobank rails, which is a distribution strategy, not a DeFi one. The trade-off is unchanged and Pharos's C+ prices it: mandatory KYC and restricted transferability sag the exit pillar to C- even as the assets behind the certificate are as boring as money gets. For institutions that need a yield product whose legal status doesn't require a creative memo from outside counsel, YLDS is still the only game in town.

sources.label: Stellar press release: Figure launches YLDS on the Stellar network
YLDS official site (rate and network availability)

usdq-quantoz.title: The Dutch Compliance Standard
usdq-quantoz.text: Quantoz's USDQ is the DNB-supervised, MiCAR-authorized e-money token that treats compliance as the product. The peg side delivers with a spotless record and zero depeg events since launch. The reserves read impeccably on paper: roughly 70% Netherlands, German, and U.S. government bonds and 30% cash at Tier 1 European banks, held in segregated bankruptcy-remote accounts at a ratio just above full backing. The catch is that Pharos has to take Quantoz's word for it. The transparency page is a self-published snapshot refreshed ad hoc, already weeks stale by the time anyone reads it, with no named auditor, no named banks, and no disclosed bond maturities. That evidence gap is why the backing pillar sits at F despite sovereign-grade assets, dragging an otherwise clean profile down to a middling overall grade. Distribution remains an afterthought too, with sub-$10M circulating across Ethereum, Polygon, XRPL, and Algorand. The lesson USDQ teaches the whole MiCAR cohort is uncomfortable: a regulator's blessing is not an attestation, and Pharos grades the evidence, not the license.

sources.label: DNB public register: Quantoz Payments B.V.

usdn-noble.title: Noble Rebasing T-Bill Dollar
usdn-noble.text: Noble's USDN is a rebasing dollar backed by M0's short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} structure, with collateral maintained by M0 minters and verified through on-chain {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}. That is a far more conventional reserve story than its Cosmos-native wrapper suggests: holders receive the accumulated T-bill yield while the protocol tracks their principal against M0's rebasing multiplier. The problem is USDN's need for demand, usable exits, and confidence in a layered bridge-and-minter arrangement, even though the collateral does not read like a casino chip. A stable peg can coexist with a very small market, because quiet is not the same thing as liquid. USDN is credible infrastructure looking for a reason not to be merely transit capital.

usdu-unitas.title: The JLP Hedge Fund
usdu-unitas.text: Unitas's USDu routes 80% of USDC deposits into Jupiter LP tokens hedged by CEX perpetual shorts through Copper and Ceffu, a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} dressed up as a stablecoin. Unitas routes 80% of USDC deposits into Jupiter LP tokens, a basket of BTC, ETH, SOL, and USDC earning Jupiter Perps trading fees, while hedging the spot exposure with CEX {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} shorts through Copper and Ceffu off-exchange {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} settlement. The remaining 20% sits as margin for the short positions, making the entire reserve an active trading strategy with exotic collateral quality classification and zero idle assets. Singapore-domiciled with Accountable providing real-time zero-knowledge solvency proofs, USDu's transparency is a genuine upgrade over the 'trust us' school of yield products. Deployed on BSC and Solana with a peg score of 99 and only six depeg events, the machinery works. The 80% dependency on USDC means every dollar of backing passes through Circle before reaching Jupiter's perps market, adding a layer of counterparty risk the hedge fund framing might obscure.

mnee-mnee.title: Clean Reserves, No Price Feed
mnee-mnee.text: MNEE was Pharos's standing proof that a fiat-backed stablecoin can hold pristine reserves, including short-dated {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}} plus cash attested by Wolf and Company, and still fail at everything surrounding them. Antigua licensing, institutional-unregulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and a single Ethereum deployment with virtually no DEX depth left the issuer API as the only credible exit, and the coin graded like a mid-tier product despite the clean balance sheet. Then listed venues went quiet enough that no usable price feed survived, and in July 2026 Pharos terminated tracking outright, retiring MNEE alongside a small batch of unpriceable assets rather than freezing it. A dollar whose market price cannot be observed is not analyzable, whatever its reserves say. The reserves may still be immaculate somewhere, but a stablecoin you cannot price is a claim, not a currency.

usdg-paxos.title: Paxos's Singapore Sequel
usdg-paxos.text: Paxos's USDG is the Singapore sequel under MAS supervision, with all-very-low-risk reserves at DBS and Standard Chartered and a dual-jurisdiction MiCA EU issuance no competitor matches. After Binance's BUSD died under regulatory fire, Paxos relocated its stablecoin ambitions to Singapore, where USDG now sits under a MAS Major Payment Institution license with reserves split between DBS Bank and Standard Chartered. Institutional-top {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} matches Circle and exceeds Tether. The v9 report card splits along institutional lines. It gives top marks on backing and an A- on economic control, but the exit pillar sits a rung lower in B territory, and the peg multiplier still discounts a brief tracking history whose early growing pains read as friction rather than structural fragility; together they hold the overall grade a notch below the leaderboard's summit. The zero-fee {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and additional EU issuance via a MiCA-compliant Finnish entity give USDG a dual-jurisdiction strategy that no competitor currently matches. The pedigree now includes card rails: Mastercard's June settlement expansion put USDG, alongside its Paxos siblings PYUSD and USDP, into the set of regulated stablecoins eligible to settle card obligations across its network. The catch is on-chain presence: concentrated on just a few chains with modest DEX depth, USDG's institutional pedigree still outpaces its DeFi footprint.

xsgd-straitsx.title: Southeast Asia's FX Shortcut
xsgd-straitsx.text: XSGD is the rare non-USD stablecoin that exists for a reason beyond novelty. It provides SGD-denominated on-chain liquidity for Southeast Asian payment flows where routing through dollar pairs adds pointless FX friction. The A is earned: a MAS Major Payment Institution licence, segregated trust reserves explicitly excluded from the issuer's creditor estate, and twice-monthly independent examinations by KK Yap & Associates, most recently on the end-June position. Backing is the one pillar trailing the rest of the card, and the reason is disclosure rather than risk: the reserve is no longer plain bank cash but close to an even split between cash and a short-dated MAS bill or eligible overnight repo category the report declines to break apart, with the safeguarding institution left unnamed. That is a rounding error in risk terms and a fair prompt for better disclosure, since half the backing is currently described by the bucket it is permitted to sit in rather than what it holds. Past oracle-driven wobbles, the inherent hazard of pricing an SGD token against USD-denominated feeds on thin non-USD pairs, have mostly aged out, and genuine DEX depth spread across many pools rather than one fragile venue keeps XSGD attached to a payment use case most stablecoins only write blog posts about.

sources.label: KK Yap & Associates XSGD SCS Reserve Account Report, 30 June 2026

xusd-straitsx.title: One Pool Holds Everything
xusd-straitsx.text:
Same MAS framework as XSGD, but a single dominant DEX pool against tens of millions in supply makes XUSD institutional plumbing without an on-chain audience.

StraitsX's XUSD inherits the same MAS framework, DBS/StanChart/UOB {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and institutional-grade infrastructure as its XSGD sibling, with semi-monthly reserve {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} still arriving on schedule. The most recent covered the end-June position. The overall C+ tells the real story: a near-flawless peg and top-grade backing dragged down by an exit pillar deep in D territory. One pool holds essentially everything, and the more than a hundred brief, mostly shallow depeg blips on record are exactly what thin markets produce. The circulating supply is respectable for a Singapore-issued dollar stablecoin, but it lives almost entirely off-chain. The on-chain footprint across its deployments is a ghost town. Stress signals rarely stray from the calm end of the scale and the backing and economic-control pillars both grade in the A range, confirming the institutional plumbing works fine; the problem is that nobody building in DeFi has a reason to choose it over USDC. The value proposition is regional FX corridors and StraitsX's banking relationships, not DEX composability. The business is valid, but it does not show up in on-chain metrics.

sources.label: KK Yap & Associates XUSD SCS Reserve Account Report, 30 June 2026

vgbp-vnx.title: Twenty Pounds in Existence
vgbp-vnx.text: VNX's Liechtenstein-licensed pound was always a thin market; by the data's account it is now not a market at all. Pharos quarantined VGBP on 2026-07-19 after DefiLlama's supply feed reported zero circulating tokens, a condition no active listing can survive. The formal scaffolding that once flattered it reads differently in this light: the latest AREVA fiat-series report, dated end-2024 and never refreshed since, attested a grand total of 20.00 VGBP in existence, while issuance quietly migrated from VNX Commodities AG to a Bermuda-licensed VNX Global entity that report does not cover. Same-day issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and TVTG licensing remain on paper, but a sterling rail with no measurable supply and a stalled {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} cycle is settlement infrastructure for settlements that are not happening. The UK regulatory wildcard now cuts the other way: if banks ever bring serious sterling liquidity on-chain, they will arrive to find the first mover already gone quiet. VGBP stays in quarantine until someone shows up holding it.

sources.label: AREVA VNX reserve report as of December 31, 2024

cusd-cap.title: Five Stablecoins, One Wrapper
cusd-cap.text: cUSD is Cap's diversified basket of regulated stablecoins and tokenized T-bill funds. Its distribution is clever if everything works, but one component failure creates shared contagion. Cap's cUSD is a basket wrapper backed by 35% USDC, 25% USDT, 20% BlackRock's BUIDL, 10% WisdomTree's WTGXX, and 10% PayPal's PYUSD: five institutional-grade stablecoins blended into a single token with a maximum 40% concentration cap per asset. The dynamic-fee vault mechanism adjusts minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} costs in real-time to prevent full utilization, ensuring atomic redemptions remain available, while EigenLayer AVS provides the economic security layer. Redemptions return a proportional basket of all underlying assets rather than a single stablecoin, which socializes any individual reserve depeg across all redeemers: clever risk distribution if everything works, shared contagion if one component fails. Deployed on Ethereum and MegaETH with wrapper-classified governance, cUSD is less an independent stablecoin and more a diversification instrument for holders who want institutional {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} exposure without choosing sides. Cap itself decentralized a notch in late June, launching its CAP governance token after a heavily oversubscribed auction. The BUIDL and WTGXX slices are tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market funds{{/term}}.

msusd-main-street.title: Redemption Target, Not A Clean Vault
msusd-main-street.text: msUSD is Main Street's dollar token with a USDC redemption target, but Pharos no longer treats it as a clean USDC reserve passthrough. Main Street documents 1:1 USDC minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} for verified users, yet the redemption path is capacity-managed, cooldown-bound, and can require position unwinds, asset conversion, and strategy liquidity before settlement. The separate msY token still owns the explicit options-box {{term:yield-bearing}}yield{{/term}} wrapper, but that split does not independently verify that unstaked msUSD is segregated from liquidity needed to support the strategy. The June 2026 depeg made that distinction material, so Pharos models msUSD with unresolved reserve-verification risk and very-high-risk reserve exposure rather than as fully backed idle USDC.

iusd-infinifi.title: Credit Book Behind a Redemption Queue
iusd-infinifi.text: USDC-collateralized dollar with duration-matched private credit deployment: a liquid buffer available on demand, the rest in credit strategies with multi-week unwinds, and redemptions queued under stress. InfiniFi's iUSD routes USDC into institutional private credit from Fasanara, FalconX, Sentora, and Maple, behind a liquid DeFi buffer on Spark, Fluid, and Aave, with the siUSD savings wrapper passing through the yield. The structural tension the model was always going to face shows up exactly where the V9 report card says it should: the backing pillar earns respectable credit and the control surface passes, but the exit pillar fails outright and drags the overall grade to a D because most of the collateral cannot be pulled on demand, whatever the mint contract promises. The peg itself holds cleanly and iUSD rarely strays from the calm end of the stress scale, but a flat stress reading is cold comfort when the real risk is a liquidity wall, not a price wobble. No depeg events recorded yet, which either means the queue is doing exactly its job or that the redemption test that matters has not arrived. Functionally siUSD is a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper over private-credit {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} positions, with the buffer-driven {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} queue acting as the gate when liquid reserves run thin. You are earning credit fund returns and bearing credit fund risks through a stablecoin interface.

pht-pht.title: Peso Stablecoin Pioneer
pht-pht.text: PHT is APACX's Philippine-peso stablecoin built like a Maker-style CDP system, but the beta reserve reality is narrower than the architecture brochure. Current Pharos metadata points to apcxUSDT wrapper collateral as the live reserve line, with apcxUSDC described as planned rather than a proven second leg. That leaves holders with USDT dependency, custodial-wrapper risk, and unresolved privileged mint or admin risk sitting behind a familiar overcollateralized label. The Chainlink PHP/USD oracle and Dutch-auction liquidation design make the mechanism legible, yet the proof path is still thin for a product asking users to trust a new local-currency peg. It is a useful experiment in peso-denominated DeFi rails, but the dashboard reads it as early machinery, not mature monetary infrastructure.

hyusd-hylo.title: Volatility Sold Separately
hyusd-hylo.text: Hylo's HYUSD is the stable tranche of a dual-token design in which each pool's xASSET absorbs collateral-price swings before HYUSD holders take any. Leverage buyers do the unpleasant work, by construction. The disclosure gap that once separated Hylo's documented V2 from its deployed program has closed: V2 is live in production with isolated SOL-LST, cbBTC, and USDC pools, and its xAsset Engine has already shipped a 3x bitcoin product, with leveraged equities still ambition rather than deployment. Pharos now measures the deployed pools directly, and the report card shows a solid backing pillar and restrained holder controls, but a failing exit pillar because on-chain liquidity for the stable tranche remains far thinner than the mechanism deserves. The peg record is nearly spotless, though the stress gauge has lately sat a notch above calm. This is a reminder that {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} via volatility-absorbing tranches is only as sturdy as the leverage demand funding it. The design finally matches its own documentation; the order books have yet to match the design.

meusd-mezo.title: Liquity Mechanics, Off-Chain Admin Keys
meusd-mezo.text: Liquity-style BTC-backed CDP stablecoin on Mezo's Bitcoin L2 with genuinely sound redemption mechanics, held in D-grade territory by a failing economic-control pillar; persistent above-peg drift from defensive overcollateralization. Mezo's meUSD applies Liquity-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics to Bitcoin collateral at a 110% minimum ratio, with permissionless {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at 75 bps and atomic settlement. These mechanics operate across native and wrapped BTC variants on a Bitcoin L2 that Pharos classifies as unproven. The v9 headline D grade tells a lopsided story: the exit pillar earns a strong B+ on those redemption mechanics and backing holds a middling C, but economic control fails outright. The Ethereum surface runs through a 5/9 Safe and a Wormhole NTT manager that can raise its own mint cap, so permissionless borrowing on Mezo coexists with very real admin keys off-chain, and v9 prices that mint authority as the dominant risk. The peg drifts above par in the way BTC-backed CDPs tend to. Borrowers overcollateralize defensively when Bitcoin volatility spikes, and meUSD has logged hundreds of brief deviation events, nearly all skewing upward. A design this sturdy deserves a better control room than it currently has.

usdu-usdu-finance.title: Undercollateralized by Design
usdu-usdu-finance.text: USDU Finance was refreshingly honest about what it was: an intentionally undercollateralized stablecoin at roughly 40% backing, minted through DAO-approved adapters connected to Curve, TermMax, and Morpho vault positions, designed explicitly for professional market participants who could price the risk. Apparently they priced it. Supply has since been all but wound down in a sharp, near-total contraction, and the issuer's transparency endpoint now reports backing roughly equal to the little that remains outstanding. The {{grade}} safety grade reflects v9's refusal to grade on a curve: a nearly empty book is easy to cover one-for-one, but an economic-control pillar with effectively unbounded mint authority and no applicable peg or supply floor keeps the arithmetic from flattering anyone. The modular adapter architecture was genuinely interesting engineering: dynamic Curve liquidity management, fixed-rate TermMax lending, and Morpho vault integration. Building sophisticated infrastructure around a product that deliberately skipped the {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} step is the kind of experiment that works until it doesn't. USDU's distinction is ending in the rare exit lane: wound down in orderly fashion before the market could write the depeg headline.

uty-xsy.title: Pristine Peg, Padlocked Exit
uty-xsy.text: XSY's UTY is an AVAX-hedged {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar custodied at Ceffu and Copper with a 7-day unbonding, and the scoreboard has finally rendered a verdict where it once shrugged: Safety Score v9 now grades it a D overall, and the pillar spread tells the whole story. The peg pillar earns an A+. The {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} of long AVAX spot against short perps with a USDC buffer holds the dollar line, and its dozens of recorded deviations are shallow blips rather than crises. Backing sits mid-C on exotic, exchange-custodied collateral attested in real time by Accountable, while economic control is a respectable B. The exit pillar is the F that anchors the grade: a 7-day unbonding period plus thin, fallback-class DEX coverage makes getting out an exercise in patience precisely when patience is most expensive. DEWS now hovers in the watch band rather than calm, which for a coin this thinly traded reads less as alarm than ambient unease. The peg mechanism evidently works whenever anyone tests it. The exit is where the grade and the risk actually live.

gusd-gate.title: Par Price, Opaque Ledger
gusd-gate.text: GUSD is Gate's account-linked yield certificate: users subscribe 1:1 with USDT, USDC, or USD1, receive daily GUSD rewards, and {{term:redemption}}redeem{{/term}} through Gate. Gate says tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}} and stablecoins back the product, but publishes no holdings schedule, named backing-asset custody structure, legal segregation, or independent reserve-to-token reconciliation. Its exchange proof-of-reserves now publishes customer and platform GUSD balances, which answers whether Gate holds customer GUSD but does not show what backs every token. The Ethereum control plane remains a single-EOA minter plus a separate no-delay EOA upgrader. GUSD also exists on GateLayer, although Pharos contract telemetry currently covers Ethereum only. The displayed market cap inherits DefiLlama's full Ethereum token-supply series and is materially above Gate subscription and CoinGecko circulating figures, so it should not be read as reconciled circulation. The peg has stayed close to par; the F reflects the evidence and control plane behind that price.

usdcv-societe-generale-forge.title: SocGen-FORGE USDCV Bank-Issued Dollar
usdcv-societe-generale-forge.text: SocGen-FORGE's USDCV is MiCA-regulated bank-issued plumbing with cash at BNY Mellon, institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and stress readings that have usually looked almost comically calm. It is what happens when one of Europe's largest banks decides to issue a stablecoin: 100% USD cash in bankruptcy-remote segregated accounts, an ACPR-regulated EMI license, and daily self-reported reserve disclosure. The live grade now sits a notch below the old headline because reach matters: two-chain deployment, concentrated DEX liquidity, and multi-day settlement through SG-FORGE's issuer portal limit the on-chain usefulness. The peg record is still one of the cleaner ones in the dashboard, which is exactly what the reserve design was built to deliver. The tension is distribution, not solvency. TradFi brought excellent paperwork on-chain, then discovered the market does not automatically provide liquidity as a courtesy.

usdai-usd-ai.title: The Liquid Base Token
usdai-usd-ai.text: USDai is the non-yielding base token in USD.AI, and the important current detail is that Pharos metadata shows the base reserve as 100% PYUSD held by the USDai contract. USDC and USDT are deposit and exit currencies for users, not the assets currently sitting underneath the base token, which is exactly the kind of distinction stablecoin marketing tends to blur when nobody is watching. The GPU-backed loan book belongs to sUSDai, the separate staking sleeve, so base USDai holders are taking PYUSD dependency and platform-admin risk rather than AI-credit yield risk. The real-time proof-of-reserves API is a genuine transparency upgrade, especially for a young product spread across multiple chains. The catch is centralized mint and upgrade control through bridge/admin roles and a Safe-governed path, so the base token is liquid and observable, not permissionless.

susdai-usd-ai.title: The GPU-Credit Sleeve
susdai-usd-ai.text: sUSDai is where USD.AI moves from a PYUSD-backed base dollar into the actual AI-credit bet. The reserve stack currently combines a large PYUSD liquid sleeve with a smaller but meaningful GPU-backed infrastructure-loan sleeve, so the token behaves like a NAV-appreciating credit product rather than a clean payment stablecoin. Accountable-style real-time reserve visibility helps separate the liquid assets from the loan book, which is useful because GPU collateral is not cash no matter how fashionable the acronym is. Exits run through staking mechanics and a queued withdrawal flow, not a simple always-on issuer redemption promise. The exit story improved at the margin in June, when USD.AI stood up a $100 million liquidity facility with Fluid, a real secondary venue, though a facility is a buffer, not a bottomless bid. sUSDai may be the interesting product in the USD.AI pair, but it is also where the yield stops being free and starts being underwriting.

usx-solstice.title: The Solana Wrapper
usx-solstice.text: Solstice's USX is a Solana wrapper minted 1:1 against 55% USDC and 45% USDT, with Chainlink Proof of Reserve and KYC-gated institutional minting. USX inherits its underlying stablecoins' safety rather than creating its own. Solstice's USX is structurally simpler than its Swiss pedigree and Galaxy Digital backing might suggest: 55% USDC and 45% USDT, minted 1:1, with Chainlink Proof of Reserve verifying the reserves on-chain. Classified as a wrapper with governance quality reflecting its pass-through nature, USX inherits the safety profile of its underlying stablecoins rather than creating its own. This makes the value proposition a question of Solana-native convenience rather than novel design. The KYC-gated institutional minting at a $500K minimum coexists with permissionless DEX access, creating a two-tier system where large minters get direct access and everyone else trades the secondary market. Plans to expand collateral to SOL, ETH, and BTC would change the risk profile entirely, but USX is currently a regulated stablecoin wrapper on a chain that already has USDC and USDT.

hollar-hydrated.title: Aave Fork, Polkadot Address
hollar-hydrated.text: HOLLAR is an Aave V3 fork on Hydration with diversified DOT, ETH, BTC, and stablecoin collateral plus HSM-anchored peg swaps. The core mechanics are a multi-collateral {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} with per-block partial {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}}, {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}, and a Stability Module that behaves like a {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}. That design earns structural credit, but everything runs on a chain Pharos still treats as unproven, which caps the ceiling no matter how tidy the fork looks. The live profile has slipped slightly, mostly because concentrated DEX liquidity and small-market demand leave the peg with little shock absorption. HOLLAR's viability ultimately tracks whether Polkadot DeFi expands or contracts. That bet has not paid off for most Polkadot-native projects to date. The product is more coherent than the ecosystem around it, which is not the comfort its holders probably wanted.

musd-metamask.title: Distribution as Moat
musd-metamask.text: MetaMask mUSD is what happens when crypto's default self-custody wallet decides to vertically integrate. It is issued by Stripe's Bridge on M0 protocol rails, with 85% in {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and 15% in bankruptcy-remote cash verified by real-time on-chain {{term:attestation}}validator attestations{{/term}}. The C safety grade is a split decision: a solid {{grade}} backing pillar and near-flawless peg behavior that rarely leaves the calm end of the stress scale, dragged down by an exit pillar that grades D. The secondary market hasn't caught up with primary-market confidence, and DEX liquidity stays spread wide and shallow. The reserve composition reads like a compliance team's wishlist, but a modest tally of brief depeg blips, including a sharp positive spike, shows that arbitrage works in theory while depth stays thin in practice. The funnel switched on at the end of June: MetaMask's Money Account wires mUSD into yield routes and card spending directly inside the wallet, the first serious attempt to convert wallet distribution into float. The moat narrative is still more aspiration than balance sheet, but the infrastructure to realize it now exists.

cash-phantom.title: The Wallet's Dollar
cash-phantom.text: CASH is Phantom's wallet-native dollar on Solana, issued through Stripe's Bridge: a distribution edge no DeFi protocol can replicate, putting a default stablecoin in front of millions of wallet users with supply now in nine figures. The distribution keeps compounding: World, the on-chain prediction market that replaced Phantom's Kalshi integration, settles winning positions automatically in CASH: the clearest sign Phantom wants CASH as the unit of account for everything the wallet touches. The report card, though, has turned brutal: the peg behaves impeccably and sits at the calm end of the stress scale, but Bridge discloses only an eligible-asset envelope: short-dated {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, Treasury repo, {{term:money-market-fund}}government money-market funds{{/term}}, and deposits in bankruptcy-remote {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at BlackRock and Fidelity, with no published category weights and no dated independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, and its reserve APIs sit behind credentials. Add exit depth that is modest for the supply on a single chain, plus issuer control as centralized as it gets, and the overall grade collapses to a failing mark despite a near-perfect peg score. A dollar can trade flawlessly and still be unverifiable; Pharos grades the evidence, not the vibes.

sources.label: BeInCrypto: World prediction market goes live in Phantom, settling in CASH (July 2026)
Bridge Building Inc. stablecoin terms (reserve envelope)

tgbp-tokenised.title: Tokenised GBP Stablecoin
tgbp-tokenised.text: tGBP is a pound stablecoin with the sensible reserve mix you would expect from a UK-facing issuer: GBP cash, money-market exposure, and short-term government paper. BCP Technologies' FCA cryptoasset registration and monthly independent attestation give the product more institutional shape than the average local-currency stablecoin. The tradeoff is not reserve exoticism but issuer centralization, since mint, burn, and upgrade control still sit behind a highly concentrated owner path. Redemption is a direct off-chain GBP workflow, which is appropriate for sterling rails and less composable than DeFi users usually pretend they want. In a market full of dollar clones, tGBP is refreshingly specific; the remaining issue is whether UK demand is large enough to make that specificity matter.

eurau-allunity.title: Deutsche Boerse's Euro Bet
eurau-allunity.text: EURAU is AllUnity's MiCA-licensed EUR stablecoin; full-reserve bank deposits, broad L2 reach, top-tier institutional sponsorship. AllUnity's EURAU is backed 100% by euro deposits at CRR-eligible EU credit institutions, BaFin-licensed as an EMI under MiCA, with institutional-regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and integration into Deutsche Boerse's Clearstream infrastructure, more institutional credibility than most euro stablecoins combined. Backed by DWS (Deutsche Bank's asset management arm), Galaxy Digital, and Flow Traders, the sponsor list reads like a TradFi-crypto {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} roster. Deployed across five EVM chains (Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon), EURAU has broader L2 reach than competing euro stablecoins that remain Ethereum-only. The problem is the denominator: euro stablecoins represent a fraction of the global stablecoin market, making EURAU simultaneously one of the best-backed euro tokens and a reminder of how thoroughly the dollar dominates this space. Direct 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through AllUnity.

usdh-native-markets.title: The Evacuated Beachhead
usdh-native-markets.text: Native Markets' USDH on HyperEVM is a Bridge-issued (Stripe) dollar with 40% short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} at JP Morgan plus tokenized treasuries. It was a bet on Hyperliquid traction that ended in a structured wind-down. USDH built to nine figures on HyperEVM with one of the more credible reserve compositions in the market: 40% short-term T-bills managed by BlackRock at JP Morgan, 20% tokenized {{term:treasury}}treasuries{{/term}} via BUIDL and USTB, and the rest in cash, repos, and {{term:money-market-fund}}treasury funds{{/term}}. All of it flowed through Bridge Building Inc., Stripe's stablecoin subsidiary. The 12 depeg events with swings as wide as 227 basis points tell the story of a young stablecoin on a single chain still building the arbitrage infrastructure to enforce its peg tightly. The bet did not get to play out: in late May Native Markets announced a structured wind-down as Coinbase took over as Hyperliquid's official USDC treasury deployer, the deployer liquidated its unlocked HYPE allocation, and by mid-June USDH's markets were settled and delisted. The validator vote that chose USDH over Paxos and Ethena was a bet on revenue redirection from Circle; the ecosystem re-voted with its treasury, and the beachhead is being evacuated in orderly fashion.

sbc-brale.title: Infrastructure Demo Reel
sbc-brale.text:
Brale's SBC is a reference implementation for its stablecoin-as-a-service platform, not a consumer product. Both the supply curve and the report card now read like a demo rather than a market.

The peg holds and the stress readings stay calm. The depeg log is a series of brief blips rather than crises. The overall grade sits in C- territory with the backing and exit pillars both in the D range. Exit suffers because an eleven-chain footprint spreads already-thin DEX liquidity thinner still, despite broader distribution than tokens fifty times its size; backing suffers because the reserve paper trail has gone soft, with the newest independently examined {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} covering May 2026 and more recent figures resting on management assertion from a niche accounting firm. The collateral story remains conservative on paper: cash and short-duration {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}} in segregated accounts from a FinCEN-registered money transmitter with zero-fee {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, which makes the attestation staleness the avoidable part. The spring growth spurt has fully unwound, with circulation back in the low single-digit millions, even as the enterprise conversations continued, including Visa's June proof-of-concept exploring SBC-based settlement on Canton. Distribution breadth was never the same thing as liquidity depth; it turns out it isn't the same thing as durable demand either.

sources.label: MCCPA SBC Reserve Attestation Report - May 2026

euri-banking-circle.title: The Binance Distribution Play
euri-banking-circle.text: EURI is Banking Circle's MiCA-licensed euro stablecoin with fee-free 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}: a {{term:custody}}credit-institution{{/term}} wrapper engineered for Binance distribution. Eurite exists because Binance needed a MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin and Banking Circle had the Luxembourg CSSF credit institution license to provide one. Holder funds sit in a segregated, bankruptcy-remote fiduciary estate of euro cash and low-risk cash equivalents, the regulatory structure arranged correctly on paper. Look for the receipts, though, and the evidence is thinner than it appears: the homepage's 'trusted attestation by a top tier auditor' links to no document, the only EY artefact on record is the bank's own financial-statements audit that mentions EURI once, and no dated reserve composition has ever been published, which is how a licensed bank's stablecoin ends up with a D on the backing pillar. The peg itself behaves well: its score is near-perfect, stress readings are parked at the calm end of the scale, and only a couple of brief blips are on record. Exit grades just as poorly as backing, because Binance's endorsement has never translated into organic on-chain trading depth on either of its two chains, Ethereum and BSC. The overall D grade tells the story: Eurite is less a standalone stablecoin than a compliance wrapper that lets Binance's European users stay in euros without leaving the exchange's orbit, and asks them to take the reserves on faith.

msusd-metronome.title: Latency Ate the Backing
msusd-metronome.text: Metronome's msUSD spent years as the durable niche synth, minted against USDC, DAI, ETH, WBTC, and Vesper yield tokens through {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}, with no direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and a peg defended by zero-slippage internal synth swaps. In late July 2026, the accounting failure surfaced: that same swap module had accumulated unbacked float because Chainlink price latency at swap execution was never covered by the fee design. Roughly 4.6 million msUSD and synthetic LPs, about 30% globally, had no debt positions behind them. The market repriced the discovery; the token broke well below par, and Pharos now shows a failing peg grade, a long tally of depeg events, and a WATCH stress band on a coin once notable for quiet persistence. The remediation plan uses fee hikes, treasury-funded loops, and systematic buyback-and-burn to re-back the float faster than holders leave. The circularity was always the design: price support depends on insiders finding the balance-sheet trade worth taking. It turns out the balance sheet itself had been miscounted for over a year.

aznd-mu-digital.title: Asia Credit in a Token
aznd-mu-digital.text: AZND is Mu Digital's KYC-gated dollar token backed by a Singapore-regulated Asia credit fund, with yield routed through the loAZND vault and a muBOND junior tranche providing {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} and absorbing first losses. It is structured credit dressed as a stablecoin. The last Accountable snapshot Pharos ingested showed the Asset Pool parked in short-term cash and liquid bonds, a notably more conservative posture than the published mandate that permits up to 20% illiquid private credit. The report card has slid to an F, and the discount is earned where it matters most: the exit and economic control pillars both bottom out, because thin Monad DEX liquidity plus weekly KYC-gated {{term:redemption}}redemptions{{/term}} settling on a fund calendar leave holders no fast path back to dollars, and Pharos stress telemetry has been running elevated. The peg score is perfect, but that is the faint praise of a peg too illiquid to be seriously tested. AZND targets a real gap in institutional Asian credit exposure on-chain. The question remains whether DeFi-native capital will accept fund-style lockups for single-digit yields.

nect-beraborrow.title: Below Redemption Scale on Berachain
nect-beraborrow.text: Liquity v2-style CDP stablecoin on Berachain backed by an exotic collateral zoo (iBGT, WBERA, BTC/ETH derivatives, LP tokens); sub-million supply and razor-thin liquidity stop the redemption mechanism from doing its job. BeraBorrow's NECT runs Liquity-v2 {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics on Berachain's exotic collateral zoo: iBGT, WBERA, wrapped BTC variants, ETH derivatives, and Kodiak LP tokens, all classified high-risk on an unproven chain. The D overall grade is earned, not harsh: NECT has logged hundreds of brief sub-peg blips with a worst deviation past 750 bps, and while the acute episodes have cooled since the May lows, the token still spends more time a point or two shy of a full dollar than parked at it. With circulating supply now down in the hundreds of thousands and thin DEX liquidity, the coin sits below the threshold where the CDP {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} mechanism can function as designed only when arbitrageurs show up; the economics don't justify it at this scale. The collateral-redemption backstop and {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} buffer remain structurally sound on paper, but sound mechanisms need liquid markets to express themselves.

usp-pikudao.title: Turkish Carry Trade, Tokenized
usp-pikudao.text: PikuDAO's USP is a NAV-appreciating token with 50% in a Turkish lira {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} via Balsa Technologies, 40% in DeFi protocols, and 10% in stablecoin buffer. Minting and redemption are KYC-gated with a whitelisted queue. PikuDAO's USP is a NAV-appreciating token. It has 50% deployed into a Turkish lira FX arbitrage strategy via Balsa Technologies ({{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} TRY/USD trades capturing Turkey's inflation-driven {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} carry), 40% across DeFi protocols (Giza, Almanak, USD.AI, Ethena, Aave, Cap), and 10% in a USDC/USDT buffer. The very-high risk classification on the Turkish FX strategy and high risk on the DeFi allocations are reflected in the exotic collateral quality rating and a backstop of 65 with whitelisted queue-based {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at 0.2% fee. KYC/KYB is required to mint or redeem, with a 24-hour FIFO settlement queue. It's a genuinely novel yield source for DeFi: Turkish carry trade returns are uncorrelated with crypto markets. It also concentrates geopolitical and counterparty risk in a single emerging market whose currency has lost over 90% against the dollar in a decade. The NAV has appreciated above $1.07, which proves the strategy works when it works. Half the float has queued out inside a month, so a meaningful share of holders decided not to wait around for the answer to what happens when it doesn't.

pmusd-precious-metals.title: Gold-Backed pmUSD With Sky PSM
pmusd-precious-metals.text: Gold-backed supply paired with a sUSDS-funded {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} means pmUSD's peg defense depends on Sky Protocol staying healthy, which is a meaningful external dependency. The structure runs on two awkward logics: supply is backed by gold via RAAC's RWf(x) fork and ION.au tokenized claims, while dollar recovery relies on a PSM holding Sky's {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} savings wrapper. Arbitrageurs can swap discounted pmUSD for sUSDS at a $1 internal valuation, but the flow is one-directional and halts if sUSDS reserves fall below the module's threshold. That ties pmUSD's dollar recovery to Sky stability, which is a strange dependency for a coin whose collateral narrative begins with precious metals. That failure mode is no longer hypothetical: pmUSD is currently trading far below the dollar. The gap measures four figures in basis points, the stress gauge is at alert, and the report card has collapsed to an F while the one-directional PSM does what it can from its side of the door. Real-time Chainlink Proof of Reserves and Instruxi {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} document the gold backing with genuine rigor; gold is not necessarily the right asset to stabilize with someone else's savings-dollar plumbing.

jupusd-jupiter.title: Three Layers to Treasuries
jupusd-jupiter.text: JupUSD is Jupiter's bid to own Solana's dollar layer, backed roughly nine-to-one by Ethena's USDtb, itself a wrapper around BlackRock's BUIDL, with a USDC buffer covering the rest. The dependency chain runs JupUSD to USDtb to BUIDL to actual government bonds: pristine collateral buried under three layers of operational and counterparty risk, custodied through Porto and Anchorage. It rises from D to C on a real finding: reserves sit in named Solana token accounts any third party can read, so coverage is recomputable from chain state rather than taken on the issuer's word, and independent verification found the token slightly over-collateralised on a sub-minute refresh. The uplift arrives with a ceiling attached, though: reconciliation is credited on cadence alone, with no attestor, no attestation section, and no regulatory disclosure anywhere on the transparency surface, so the centralized-mint constraint survives and is now the binding cap on the card. A zero-delay 4-of-9 Squads multisig can replace the mint logic outright, and the monthly attestations that show up in press coverage belong to USDtb, the collateral issuer, not to JupUSD. Jupiter is betting BlackRock's brand travels well through intermediaries; Pharos will keep charging the wrapper tax until somebody signs something.

u-united-stables.title: Variable Reserve Wrapper
u-united-stables.text: United Stables' U is a BVI-issued dollar whose reserve policy is deliberately flexible: cash, U.S. Treasury bills, and approved fiat-referenced stablecoins may all sit in the basket, and the governing terms permit the mix and its counterparties to change without notice. That flexibility is operationally convenient and analytically useless, because the live feed reports one aggregate balance. There is no composition to score, only an envelope. This release does credit a genuine improvement: the proof-of-reserves path resolves to a third-party Chainlink feed with a named external auditor rather than an issuer dashboard, which is materially better than self-reporting and lifts economic control sharply. It changes the grade not at all, because the exit pillar scores zero on correlated routes, and because the same terms that describe segregated custody on the website state that United Stables need not segregate reserves and that holders hold no preferential, secured, or proprietary claim in insolvency. The marketing page and the contract you actually agree to are not describing the same product. U is trying to be a programmable reserve wrapper; the risk is that the wrapper's discretion is the product.

reusd-re-protocol.title: Insurance Capital Goes On-Chain
reusd-re-protocol.text: Re Protocol's reUSD is a NAV-appreciating token that channels deposits into ETH basis trades, short-duration T-bills, and a USDC instant-redemption buffer. The reserve split reads like reinsurance float deployed across DeFi yield sources: half the book rides on USDe and sUSDe {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} {{term:basis-trade}}basis trades{{/term}}, with Treasuries and USDC cushioning the exit path. The live grade has improved from the older summary's read, but the upgrade does not erase the central dependency: Ethena infrastructure is doing a lot of work inside the collateral stack. Multi-chain deployment and real secondary-market depth make reUSD more usable than many yield tokens wearing a dollar label. Queue-based {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, 20% immediate capacity, and BVI licensing will not satisfy conservative compliance teams, but the Chainlink/Network Firm real-time {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} layer helps. It remains one of the more intellectually honest yield products on the market, which is not the same as being simple.

rwausdi-multipli.title: The RWA Middleware Layer
rwausdi-multipli.text:
A KYB-gated UAE wrapper aggregating 100+ tokenized T-bills, gold, and market-neutral funds, with a Lloyd's de-pegging insurance policy that's a genuinely novel backstop.

Multipli's rwaUSDi wraps 100+ tokenized treasury products, gold tokens, and market-neutral fund units into a single mintable stablecoin: tokenized {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} (BUIDL, USDY, OUSG), aggregated treasury-backed stablecoins, tokenized gold, and institutional fund units from Nomura, Fasanara, and Edge Capital. The pitch is that lending protocols can't individually underwrite hundreds of {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} tokens, so rwaUSDi does the aggregation and due diligence, backed by a Lloyd's insurance policy covering de-pegging risk, which is a genuinely novel backstop for a stablecoin. The token is UAE-domiciled with AFI-audited on-chain reserves. It has spread from Ethereum across Base, Arbitrum, and Monad while keeping KYB-gated institutional minting, making it less a retail product and more a composable RWA building block.
