The peg record is clean, with no depeg events on file. The backing pillar fails under v9 because the elegant abstraction is exactly what a scoring engine cannot see through, with no current reserve composition on file and the mechanism reviews unconfirmed. A trust layer between holder and underlying assets works beautifully until someone asks to inspect the trust.

usdm-mega.title: Funding the Sequencer
usdm-mega.text: MegaETH's USDm flips the L2 business model: instead of extracting sequencer fees from users, it uses {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} yield from Ethena's USDtb (~90% of backing, itself holding BlackRock's BUIDL tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury bills{{/term}}) to subsidize network operations. The chain gets cheaper as more people hold its native stablecoin. The peg itself holds flawlessly and the asset has logged only a couple of brief deviations, with the stress gauge sitting at the quiet end of the scale, but the absence of any tracked DEX liquidity means exit routes are limited to the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} mechanism. The dependency on Ethena's infrastructure for both reserve management and {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} adds counterparty risk that the underlying Treasuries don't carry, and it shows in the grading: a C-range overall grade weighed down by weak backing and exit pillars, with a dependency profile that inherits USDtb's concentrated mint authority wholesale. The stablecoin's value proposition is inseparable from MegaETH's own traction as an L2. Stablecoin adoption subsidizes network costs, which can drive adoption. The same flywheel can also turn in the other direction.

usdm-monetrix.title: HyperEVM's USDC Wrapper
usdm-monetrix.text: Monetrix USDM is the base dollar token in a small HyperEVM yield stack: USDC backs liquid USDM, while sUSDM is the separate staking wrapper where the strategy exposure lives. That split matters because Pharos can admit USDM through DefiLlama supply plus CoinGecko pricing, but sUSDM still lacks a maintained market-cap and price source in the runtime pipeline. The reserve story is therefore straightforward but narrow: USDM inherits USDC issuer risk and Monetrix smart-contract/operations risk, while the dashboard transparency is self-reported rather than an independent attestation. It is useful coverage for HyperEVM dollar liquidity, not yet a fully modeled yield product.

usat-tether.title: Tether Goes Domestic
usat-tether.text: Tether's USA-T is a GENIUS-era U.S. dollar issued 1:1 by Anchorage Digital Bank under an OCC federal charter, backed by cash and {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}}-collateralized reverse repos with Cantor Fitzgerald {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and monthly Deloitte {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} reports. It is the cleanest regulatory setup Tether has ever assembled. The report card has caught up with the paperwork: a B+ overall on the strength of A-range backing and economic control pillars, a spotless peg with no depeg events on record, and a stress read that rarely leaves the calm end of the scale. The softest pillar is exit. Secondary-market depth on a still Ethereum-only deployment remains limited, but it has climbed from early-days thinness to a respectable B-, which is what happens when distribution starts catching up to compliance. The strategic logic is transparent: USA-T is Tether's answer to USDC on US soil, separating the domestic compliance story from USDT's offshore empire, with a 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} promise through Anchorage. Whether American institutions will trust a Tether-branded dollar after a decade of skepticism remains the open question. The scorecard no longer gives them an excuse.

yzusd-yuzu.title: A Yield Aggregator With a Dollar Peg
yzusd-yuzu.text:
A KYC-gated yield aggregator on Plasma minted 1:1 with USDT0, with a junior tranche absorbing first losses and zero secondary market to test the peg.

Yuzu's yzUSD packages curated DeFi yield strategies into an {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} stablecoin: 50% Pendle PT/LP positions, 20% Euler/Morpho lending, 20% other DeFi strategies, and a 10% USDT0 buffer. All are classified as exotic collateral on an unproven chain (Plasma). A perfect peg score and zero depeg events sound reassuring until you note the absence of any DEX liquidity and queue-based {{term:redemption}}redemptions{{/term}} scoring just 56 on the backstop, with the yzPP junior tranche absorbing first losses. Strict KYC gating means only accredited, qualified, or institutional investors can mint and redeem. This makes yzUSD one of the most access-restricted stablecoins in DeFi, which explains both the zero depeg events (few holders means few sellers) and the non-existent secondary market. It's a yield aggregator that happens to maintain a dollar peg rather than a stablecoin that happens to generate yield. The distinction matters when things go wrong.

nusd-neutrl.title: The Contraction Test
nusd-neutrl.text: Delta-neutral synthetic dollar backed mainly by stablecoins plus hedged OTC positions; weathering a deep, months-long supply contraction without breaking peg, with whitelisted queue-based redemption and a yield-bearing sNUSD wrapper. Neutrl's NUSD has been stress-tested by something more revealing than a depeg event: a contraction that has now erased roughly three-quarters of its peak supply, as holders queue for the exit month after month. The {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar, backed overwhelmingly by stablecoin reserves with OTC and hedged {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} positions in a {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} structure, has held its peg cleanly through the drawdown, with only a handful of shallow sub-200-bps blips on record, which says more about the mechanism than any bull-market AUM figure could. The composite grade slipped while the outflow was at its worst and has recovered only to a C+. The dashboard credits clean redemption processing while declining to applaud a product whose base is still draining. The durable constraint is the shrinking base: a clean exit queue cannot establish that the product will retain scale when it clears.

usdgo-osl.title: A Billion in Three Months
usdgo-osl.text: OSL's USDGO has been compounding supply at a pace that makes most stablecoin launches look lethargic, backed by T-bills and cash at Anchorage Digital under an OCC charter. On-chain liquidity is the bottleneck, not credentials. The float crossed the ten-figure line in July 2026. OSL says the run from $100 million to $1 billion took three months, placing USDGO among the top six regulated stablecoins globally by circulating supply. It has kept drifting higher since, all while holding a near-perfect peg. The safety grade has settled at a C+ as on-chain liquidity strains to keep pace with issuance, but the reserve stack keeps upgrading: Treasury bills and cash under an OCC federal bank charter, now diversified across tokenized money-market funds from JPMorgan, BlackRock, and Goldman Sachs. These credentials outclass most competitors several times its size, with institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and same-day {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. Thin on-chain depth against a ten-figure float makes this an issuer-API exit story rather than an on-chain arbitrage play. The exit pillar is the report card's weak leg, with OSL's institutional pipeline doing the heavy lifting. The old question was whether the surge was one-time onboarding; a billion-dollar float built in months says the Asia-Pacific institutional pipeline is a durable bid. The remaining issue is whether the on-chain plumbing ever catches up to it.

sources.label: OSL Group: USDGO circulating supply surpasses US$1 billion (July 20, 2026)

fidd-fidelity.title: Fidelity's Chartered Dollar
fidd-fidelity.text: FIDD is Fidelity Digital Assets' OCC-chartered dollar stablecoin backed by cash and short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} at BNY Mellon: a regulatory beachhead from a multi-trillion-dollar asset manager. When Fidelity issues a stablecoin, the signal overwhelms the product, and the product is deliberately boring: 80% T-bills, 20% cash, Big Four {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, and institutional-grade {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. The live safety profile has moved higher than the old summary claimed, which makes sense for a token whose reserve quality is the least interesting risk. The off-chain {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop with same-day settlement is institutionally normal rather than crypto-native magic. Early DEX coverage suggests Fidelity is building infrastructure methodically instead of spraying liquidity incentives. FIDD's peg record is established, while Fidelity's decision to distribute the token beyond the proof-of-capability phase remains unresolved.

aid-gaib.title: GPU Yield, Dollarized
aid-gaib.text: AID is GAIB's centralized dollar stablecoin, minted 1:1 against USDC and USDT and backed by T-bills and approved stables. Its companion sAID accrues GPU/AI infrastructure financing yield. GAIB's AID is a conventional dollar stablecoin backed by {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and stablecoin reserves, with 1:1 mint and burn. Its entire reason for existing is its companion token sAID, which accrues yield from GPU and AI infrastructure financing deals. The structure neatly separates stable value (AID) from exotic yield (sAID), letting users choose their risk exposure. At $21 million market cap it's early-stage even by {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} standards, betting that AI compute demand will create a durable yield substrate. Whether GPU financing agreements produce reliable enough cash flows to back a yield product is genuinely untested, but in a market where every new stablecoin needs a narrative, "AI infrastructure yield" is at least more substantive than most.

apxusd-apyx.title: Dividends as Collateral
apxusd-apyx.text: apxUSD is Apyx's dollar stablecoin backed by preferred shares of Digital Asset Treasury companies plus a cash and {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} buffer: an experimental collateral type that bets equity dividends from crypto-holding firms can stay near par. Apyx introduced what might be the most creative collateral backing in stablecoins: preferred shares from Digital Asset Treasury companies, publicly traded equity from firms like Strategy that hold large crypto positions. The theory is that variable-rate preferred shares trade near par regardless of crypto price volatility, providing stable collateral for a dollar token. Launched on Ethereum in February 2026 with DeFi Development Corp as an early investor, apxUSD scaled to nine figures fast. Then the theory met June 2026. The answer arrived quickly: as Bitcoin fell, Strategy's STRC preferred traded below par and apxUSD followed it down, first to the $0.90s in early June, then through $0.80 by late month. The token still sits well below the dollar with the stress gauge parked at watchful and the report card reading F. The issuer calls preferred-share pass-through a feature rather than a bug, which is honest as far as it goes, but a dollar that trades at a structural discount whenever its collateral does is a tracking certificate wearing a stablecoin's clothing. Pharos treats the reserve profile as closer to {{term:rwa}}real-world-asset{{/term}} credit than to a cash-only stablecoin.

jpyc-jpyc.title: The Yen's Licensed Pioneer
jpyc-jpyc.text: Japan's first FSA-approved yen stablecoin, 100% JPY deposit and JGB-backed under a Type II Funds Transfer license; market cap still modest. Japan's first FSA-approved yen stablecoin occupies an enviable regulatory position. It has a Type II Funds Transfer license under the Payment Services Act, 100% backing in JPY deposits and Japanese government bonds, institutional-regulated custody, and zero transaction fees. Deployed across several public chains with the JPYC EX platform handling mint and redemption via bank transfer after KYC, the infrastructure is sound but circulation remains modest, which shows that regulatory compliance alone doesn't drive adoption. The competitive threat has also changed shape: while everyone watched the Progmat megabank consortium, SBI got there first. JPYSC launched in June 2026 as Japan's first trust-bank yen stablecoin, with trust-law redemption rights and a float already several times JPYC's entire supply, despite being locked inside SBI's own exchange. Pharos's report card tells the fuller story. Peg and exit are JPYC's strongest pillars, supported by bank-rail redemption and tokens that actually trade on open chains. Backing is the weakest, a gap between the license's promise and the reserve evidence Pharos can verify. The structural moat is reserves split between bank deposits and JGB {{term:treasury}}treasury bonds{{/term}}, FSA-mandated {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, institutional-regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and bank-rail {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} via JPYC EX. First-mover status is still worth something, because unlike its trust-bank rival, JPYC's yen can actually leave the building.

sources.label: Ledger Insights: SBI launches first trust bank yen stablecoin JPYSC

xaut-tether.title: Tether Mints Bullion
xaut-tether.text:
Tether's Swiss-vaulted LBMA gold token rides USDT's brand and BDO Italia attestations but is steadily losing share to PAXG's bar-level transparency.

Tether's gold token is backed 100% by LBMA Good Delivery bars in Swiss vaults with BDO Italia {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, operating under El Salvador's CNAD jurisdiction with institutional-regulated custody. It uses the same transparency framework as USDT, applied to physical bullion. XAUT commands the largest share of the tokenized gold market, which sounds impressive until you notice that share has been eroding as PAXG and newer competitors chip away at the margins. Deployed across nearly a dozen chains from Ethereum to Solana and TON, XAUT works exactly like you'd expect from Tether: a market that trades on brand recognition over the granular bar-level transparency that Paxos offers with PAXG's allocated serial numbers. Tether has meanwhile tightened the family around the flagship, winding down its Alloy platform and the XAUT-collateralized aUSDT. Holders have until mid-September to pull their gold collateral out. This indicates that the market wanted the bullion token, not derivatives of it. With gold's rally inflating all boats, XAUT's real significance may be Tether's own physical gold accumulation rather than the tokenized wrapper itself.

paxg-paxos.title: Bar Serials and Bankruptcy Remoteness
paxg-paxos.text: PAXG is Paxos's gold token with the paperwork turned all the way up: one fine troy ounce of allocated LBMA Good Delivery gold per token, Brink's London vaulting, KPMG monthly attestations, and Paxos trust supervision. In a tokenized gold market where the metal is the easy part, PAXG competes on custody traceability and regulatory comfort rather than chain sprawl. The issuer-direct mint path and centralized controls are still there, because apparently even bullion needs an admin console in 2026. The June 2026 Solana expansion finally ends the Ethereum-only era, but a two-chain footprint after seven years still tells you who the product is for: allocators who care more about bar serials and bankruptcy remoteness than the latest bridge. XAUT sells brand gravity; PAXG sells receipts.

sources.label: Paxos PAX Gold: allocation lookup covers Ethereum and Solana wallets
WEEX News: PAXG launched on Solana mainnet (June 2026)

kau-kinesis.title: Gold That Pays Rent
kau-kinesis.text: 1 gram LBMA-gold-backed token with 15% transaction-fee yield sharing and Mastercard spending; Cayman VASP, Bureau Veritas audited. Kinesis cracked the code that other gold tokens missed: people want yield. KAU holders earn a share of 15% of all platform transaction fees, paid monthly in additional gold, backed 1:1 by LBMA-approved physical gold at 1 gram per token in ABX vaults, Bureau Veritas audited, under a Cayman CIMA VASP license. Add a virtual Mastercard for point-of-sale gold spending and you get something genuinely different: gold that functions as money, not just an asset, with institutional-regulated custody and independent attestation that the bars actually exist. The catch is that yield depends entirely on Kinesis's transaction volume. If trading dries up, so does the rent check, and without any tracked on-chain contracts, KAU exists primarily within Kinesis's own platform rather than the broader DeFi ecosystem. A growing challenger to the XAUT-PAXG duopoly, betting that yield and spendability matter more than Ethereum composability. Bureau Veritas {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} verifies the bars exist at the ABX vault {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} that backs physical {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}.

xaum-matrixdock.title: Asia's Institutional Bullion
xaum-matrixdock.text:
LBMA gold vaulted in Singapore and Hong Kong with Bureau Veritas audits. The design is an Asia-domicile bet against London- and Swiss-vaulted competitors.

Matrixdock's XAUm is backed by LBMA-certified 99.99% gold bars at Brink's and Malca-Amit in Singapore and Hong Kong, Bureau Veritas audited via independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, with institutional-regulated custody and a minimum redemption of 32.148 XAUm (1 kg) restricted to KYC'd accredited investors. The Asia-Pacific custody thesis uses Singapore and Hong Kong vaults rather than London or Switzerland. It is a deliberate choice targeting institutions that prefer regional domicile for their gold exposure. The Ethereum-and-BNB-Chain token of its launch year has become a distribution play: a February 2026 Solana deployment and a Stellar launch pushed the footprint to eight networks Pharos tracks, alongside Polygon, Tron, Sui, and Plume, while Matrixdock's tokenization work for Bhutan's Gelephu Mindfulness City signals ambitions beyond retail bullion. XAUm remains a modest share of the tokenized gold market, and the report card catches the asymmetry: respectable backing and economic control against an exit pillar that reflects eight chains of distribution funneling into a single kilo-bar {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} desk. Whether institutions actually prefer Asia-domiciled custody over the London and Swiss vaults that XAUT and PAXG offer remains the strategic bet.

sources.label: Matrixdock expands XAUm to Solana (PR Newswire, Feb 2026)

cgo-comtech.title: DMCC-Stamped Bullion
cgo-comtech.text: CGO is ComTech's tokenized gold from Dubai vaults at 1 gram per token. Its local credentials are impeccable, but global adoption is negligible. ComTech Gold's CGO is backed 1:1 by 24-karat 999.9% physical gold at 1 gram per token in Transguard vaults under the Emirates Group umbrella, DMCC endorsed, with individually serialized bars registered on DMCC Tradeflow and institutional-regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} under DAFZA jurisdiction. The {{term:redemption}}redemption-via-app{{/term}} workflow with minimum 10-gram delivery is the most retail-friendly physical gold offramp in the tokenized gold market, leveraging Dubai's regulatory clarity on {{term:rwa}}tokenized commodities{{/term}} that is genuinely ahead of most jurisdictions. Without tracked on-chain contracts, CGO exists primarily within the ComTech ecosystem rather than DeFi, and none of the UAE pedigree has translated into meaningful global adoption.

dgld-gold-token-sa.title: Heritage Gold, Rebooted
dgld-gold-token-sa.text: DGLD is Gold Token SA's tokenized PAMP gold from Swiss vaults at 1 ounce per token. Its heritage is pristine, but adoption is negligible. DGLD is backed 1:1 by allocated LBMA Good Delivery PAMP gold bars at 1 troy ounce per token, with real-time reserve verification through on-chain bar serial numbers and VQF/FINMA regulatory oversight. The Swiss refiner behind the bars has a name synonymous with premium bullion. MKS PAMP relaunched DGLD in late 2025 with deployments on Ethereum and Base, institutional-regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and minimum 1-gram {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}: the lowest physical gold redemption threshold of any tokenized gold product. A 60-year refining heritage and the most prestigious gold backing in crypto have produced one of the least adopted gold tokens on the market, proving that heritage is necessary but wildly insufficient for winning the tokenized gold race. The dual-chain deployment signals ambition beyond the institutional market, but DGLD's traction remains a fraction of what PAMP's reputation would suggest. Allocated gold qualifies it as a {{term:rwa}}real-world asset{{/term}} stable.

kag-kinesis.title: The Lonely Ounce
kag-kinesis.text: KAG is a claim on one troy ounce of allocated silver, and for most of its life on Pharos it carried the word audited without anyone opening the artefact to see what that word was doing. Someone opened it. Bureau Veritas's April 2026 work is a commodity vault inspection performed under agreed procedures with no opinion expressed, scoped to assets only. It counts metal against vault records and stops there. The sole place tokens are compared to silver is the issuer's own cover letter, signed by a party who heads both Kinesis and the vault operator, which is a reconciliation in roughly the sense that a self-addressed envelope is correspondence. The score moved barely at all, and that restraint is the point: the silver is very likely in the vault and the inspection is very likely competent, but neither fact is the same as an independent party confirming that outstanding KAG is covered by it. Anyone here for the yield should know that the ERC-20 tracked on this page does not accrue Kinesis transaction-fee sharing, which belongs to native balances. Tokenized silver is still a market of approximately one, and its lone resident is now rated on what its paperwork proves rather than what the paperwork is called.

eurq-quantoz.title: The Enterprise Euro
eurq-quantoz.text: EURQ is Quantoz's DNB-supervised MiCA euro stablecoin with 102% reserves and direct SEPA integration, built for corporate {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, not DeFi. Quantoz built EURQ for corporate treasurers, not DeFi degens. It is DNB-regulated under MiCA, with 102% reserved in 68% eurozone government bonds and 32% cash at Tier 1 European banks, with direct SEPA integration and institutional-regulated custody. The same Dutch compliance infrastructure as its USDQ sibling, EURQ carves a niche in programmable corporate payments where compliance is a feature, not a tax. The 2% over-collateralization buffer and self-reported {{term:attestation}}transparency{{/term}} are a restrained signal: enough to signal conservatism without dragging capital efficiency, supervised by the same DNB that oversees ING and ABN AMRO. Whether the enterprise market actually wants an on-chain euro or just talks about it at conferences remains the open question, but Quantoz is better positioned than most to find out.

deuro-deuro.title: The Oracle-Free Euro
deuro-deuro.text: DEURO is a decentralized euro stablecoin minted from BTC/ETH/crypto vaults using oracle-free Frankencoin-style auctions; rare genuinely decentralized euro. Born from the same codebase as Frankencoin (ZCHF), dEURO takes the contrarian position that price oracles are a point of failure, not a feature; its {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} model uses internal auctions instead of external price feeds, a design that trades capital efficiency for resilience against oracle manipulation. The collateral is omnivorous: 40% WBTC, 25% WETH, 10% XAUT (tokenized gold), and smaller positions in USDC, DAI, UNI, and ZCHF, all valued through auction-based mechanisms on five chains. With governance fully transferred to token holders and no founder control over contracts, dEURO is genuinely decentralized in a euro stablecoin market where that word usually means 'we have a multisig', one of only two decentralized euro stablecoins tracked by Pharos. MiCA's evolving stance on decentralized stablecoins could be either tailwind or existential threat, depending on whether European regulators view oracle-free design as innovation or evasion. {{term:overcollateralization}}Overcollateralization{{/term}} and auction-driven {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} stand in for an oracle-fed margin call.

cetes-etherfuse.title: Three Counterparties, One Yield
cetes-etherfuse.text: CETES is Etherfuse's tokenized wrapper around Mexico's {{term:treasury}}Treasury bills{{/term}}, zero-coupon sovereign debt auctioned weekly, NAV-accreting in MXN, held through INDEVAL {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} with monthly BHR México reasonable-assurance {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} that fully reconcile assets against liabilities. The structure stacks three dependencies: the peso, the BBB- sovereign, and the issuer. FX risk for dollar-denominated holders never shows up in the {{term:yield-bearing}}yield{{/term}} headline. Deployed across five chains from Solana to Stellar behind KYC-gated minting, it offers genuine on-chain access to Mexican sovereign debt for anyone willing to do the paperwork. But since mid-July 2026 Pharos has held the token in quarantine: none of the permitted market-data sources reports a positive circulating supply or market cap, so live scoring is withheld until usable numbers reappear. A sovereign-debt {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} wrapper with verified reserves and no verifiable circulation is an odd inversion: the backing is currently easier to prove than the float.

zarp-zarp.title: The Rand's Digital Outpost
zarp-zarp.text: ZARP is backed effectively one-for-one by rand cash. The overwhelming bulk sits in an Old Mutual Wealth trust account, with a sliver at Standard Bank. ZARP remains the only meaningfully documented on-chain rand. This release moves the score without moving the grade: nine Kempen reports running from May 2024 through July 2026 were re-read and now qualify as recurring third-party reconciliation, lifting economic control substantially while ZARP stays in F. Read those reports for what they are, though. They are ISRS 4400 agreed-upon procedures that expressly state they are not an assurance engagement and express no opinion, and the July one leaves a gap of roughly R1.2 million between the balances Kempen actually verified and the single unbroken total management asserts alongside them, unreconciled anywhere in the document. The real drag sits on the exit side: no comparable same-notional route out exists, the FSCA CASP licence is still pending, and the issuer operates as a representative of another firm with no SARB endorsement. ZARP's problem was never credibility. The constraint is scale: a carefully documented rand you cannot trade at scale is still a rand you cannot trade at scale.

syrupusdc-maple.title: Institutional Lending, Vaulted
syrupusdc-maple.text: Maple's syrupUSDC turns USDC into an ERC-4626 receipt for institutional lending, a tidy way to make private credit look like a composable stablecoin. Deposits fund overcollateralized fixed-rate loans, value accrues through NAV, and withdrawals are served by a FIFO queue that can run to thirty days rather than pretending every lender can leave at once, which is why exit is comfortably the weakest pillar here and always has been. The Network Firm proof-of-reserves programme was announced in May, but the collateralization report it promised is still marked coming soon, so the transparency page currently serves live AUM where independent verification was implied. Neither of those moved the card this release: no ceiling binds it and no upstream revision touched it, so the grade is the plain weighted verdict of its own pillars, with the withdrawal queue doing all the work of keeping it out of A territory. That distinction matters. A private-credit book denominated in someone else's dollar carries two credit stories, and the one Pharos can actually score is not the one that would hurt you. Maple keeps institutionalizing the front end; the credit cycle underneath stays stubbornly analogue.

syrupusdt-maple.title: The Mirror Vault
syrupusdt-maple.text: Maple's USDT counterpart to syrupUSDC runs on identical machinery. It is an ERC-4626 vault feeding {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} fixed-rate loans to institutional borrowers, with exits served by a FIFO withdrawal queue rather than the pretense that every lender can leave at once. The old Ethereum-only caveat has expired: the vault now spans Ethereum, Plasma, BSC, Mantle, and Ink, yet it still runs at well under half of syrupUSDC's size. What actually separates the twins is the dollar underneath. Routing the same private-credit book through Tether instead of Circle costs the mirror its sibling's top-shelf backing grade and a rung on the overall card, while the withdrawal queue keeps exit the weakest pillar for both. On verification the vaults share one asterisk: Maple announced a Network Firm proof-of-reserves programme in May, but the transparency page still serves live AUM figures where the promised independent collateralization report should be: announced, not published. For yield-seekers who prefer their credit exposure denominated in Tether rather than Circle, this is the vault; just know the mirror reflects syrupUSDC a shade darker.

yousd-yield-optimizer.title: Fifty Strategies, One Token
yousd-yield-optimizer.text:
A USDC-only yield aggregator on Base whose NAV can move with strategy outcomes. It is a sophisticated optimizer wearing stablecoin clothing, not a fixed-dollar claim.

YO Protocol's yoUSD automates what DeFi power users do manually: rebalancing USDC across 50+ yield sources on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, and Unichain, ranked by risk scores with per-pool and per-protocol concentration caps. That diversification still leaves holders exposed to venue and allocator risk. The March 22 2026 Resolv exploit produced a reported ~2.95% yoUSD drawdown through Resolv-linked exposure, a useful reminder that NAV-appreciating tokens can also absorb strategy losses. Backed by Paradigm, Haun Ventures, and Coinbase Ventures, yoUSD remains a sophisticated {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} product, but the relevant question is no longer whether the NAV only climbs; it is whether the extra yield compensates for the portfolio's tail risk.

ustb-superstate.title: Wall Street's On-Chain Fund
ustb-superstate.text: USTB is a tokenized short-duration government-securities fund managed by Invesco and held at BNY Mellon, with the manners and access limits of a traditional private fund because that is what it is. The share price accrues with daily NAV rather than maintaining a fixed dollar, and qualified purchasers subscribe or redeem in USD or USDC on business days. Public holdings, daily NAV disclosure, and institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} make the underlying {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} exposure unusually legible; the restricted investor base makes open DEX liquidity beside the point. USTB matters less as a consumer {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} token than as collateral other protocols can use without building a BNY Mellon relationship. It is Wall Street's fund wrapper on-chain, which is both the innovation and the disclaimer.

ousg-ondo-finance.title: The Hundred-Dollar Stablecoin
ousg-ondo-finance.text: Ondo's tokenized U.S. T-Bill fund (mostly BlackRock BUIDL plus FedFund and a USDC buffer); NAV-accreting at north of $115 per token, KYC-restricted to U.S. Qualified Purchasers, with instant T+0 mint and redeem via USDC. OUSG holds a few hundred million dollars, currently south of $400 million, with the bulk in BlackRock's BUIDL alongside a FedFund sleeve and a small USDC liquidity buffer, keeping Ondo I LP among BUIDL's largest single holders and OUSG essentially a first-class derivative of BlackRock's tokenized {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} presence. At north of $115 per token with NAV appreciating daily, it is the least dollar-like entry on any stablecoin dashboard, which is why Ondo maintains rOUSG, a rebasing sibling that stays at $1 while OUSG accumulates. The SEC investigation closure in November 2025 without charges removed the key regulatory overhang, and the instant T+0 mint/{{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} via OUSGInstantManager against USDC through BUIDL on-chain liquidity makes OUSG's exit infrastructure better than most tokenized funds. OUSG is restricted to U.S. Qualified Purchasers with on-chain KYC enforcement, so its tokens literally cannot transfer to non-whitelisted addresses. OUSG is less a stablecoin and more a tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} that borrowed the infrastructure.

slvon-ondo.title: Silver ETF Rails
slvon-ondo.text: SLVon is Ondo Global Markets' tokenized exposure to the iShares Silver Trust, tracked as a {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} NAV asset rather than a $1 stablecoin. The token gives eligible non-U.S. investors economic exposure to SLV on Ethereum, BSC, Solana, and HyperEVM, with Ondo handling the issuer, subscription, and redemption infrastructure. The useful feature is composability for a listed ETF; the tradeoff is that holders own an Ondo GM token, not direct ETF shares or physical silver. Risk therefore lives in the Ondo GM legal structure, collateral attestations, access controls, and secondary-market liquidity.

iauon-ondo.title: Gold ETF Rails
iauon-ondo.text: IAUon is Ondo Global Markets' tokenized exposure to the iShares Gold Trust, modeled as a {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} NAV asset rather than a dollar stablecoin. It is gold-linked through the underlying IAU ETF exposure, not through direct allocated bullion redemption like PAXG or XAUT. Ondo's multi-chain issuer rails make the ETF exposure portable across Ethereum, BSC, Solana, and HyperEVM, while eligibility restrictions and issuer controls remain central to the risk profile. The cleanest way to read IAUon is as tokenized listed-security exposure that borrows stablecoin-style settlement infrastructure.

mtbill-midas.title: Europe's T-Bill Token
mtbill-midas.text: Compliance-first European tokenized U.S. T-bill product (BlackRock IB01 ETF, Swiss custody, FMA-approved MiFID II), restricted to non-U.S./UK retail; daily Ankura NAV attestations. mTBILL is Midas's compliance-first answer to the tokenized {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} race: 97% in BlackRock's IB01 ETF with Swiss {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at Maerki Baumann, issued as a Liechtenstein FMA-approved MiFID II instrument. That is the exact bureaucratic architecture required to legally sell T-bill exposure to European professionals. Ankura Trust provides daily on-chain NAV {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, and the {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} collateral quality with regulated-entity governance earns institutional credibility that most crypto-native tokenized treasury products lack. The 'not available to U.S. or UK retail persons' restriction is the mirror image of USTB and OUSG's American access gates, carving out a European institutional niche in a market dominated by U.S. issuers. Deployed across five chains, mTBILL functions as infrastructure in Midas's product stack and as stable collateral in third-party structured products. It is the European {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market-fund-like{{/term}} token for protocols that need regulatory certainty over DeFi composability.

rusd-reservoir.title: Reservoir's Base Dollar
rusd-reservoir.text: rUSD is the non-yielding base asset under Reservoir's savings tokens: mintable and redeemable 1:1 for USDC, USDT, or USD1, but backed by a protocol balance sheet that also routes capital into lending markets and credit strategies. The live reserve feed makes the dependency stack visible, with current exposure concentrated in RLUSD and GHO lending markets plus smaller USDC, AUSD, USD1, and PYUSD slices. That gives rUSD more transparency than a black-box credit book, but it also means the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} promise depends on multiple upstream stablecoin issuers, DeFi venues, and Reservoir governance rather than a simple cash account.

wsrusd-reservoir.title: Rebuilt After a $285M Run
wsrusd-reservoir.text:
Reservoir's ERC-4626 NAV vault survived a $285M bank run, then reincarnated as a seven-stablecoin reserve managed by named curators with enforced solvency floors.

Reservoir's rUSD processed $285M in redemptions 'without failure' in November 2025, then flatlined. The protocol survived a bank run while losing the patient. The reincarnation as wsrUSD is an ERC-4626 NAV vault backed by an unusually varied diet: 30% USDC, 25% USDT, 10% PYUSD, 5% GHO, 5% RLUSD, 5% USD1, plus strategy vaults and lending markets: seven upstream stablecoin dependencies curated by Steakhouse, Gauntlet, and other named managers. Credit Enforcer smart contracts enforce minimum 105% liquidity, solvency, and capital ratios before any leverage-increasing action, which is the kind of on-chain risk management that most {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} protocols skip. Deployed across 15 chains with exotic collateral quality and multisig governance, wsrUSD's flexibility is genuine, but the seven-dependency architecture means the protocol's safety is a derivative of Circle, Tether, PayPal, Aave, Ripple, and World Liberty Financial simultaneously.

dusd-alto.title: The Isolated Vault Stablecoin
dusd-alto.text: DUSD is Alto's {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style dollar. It is minted from isolated Ethereum markets for ETH and LSTs, sUSDe, and Syrup USDC, each ring-fenced with per-asset risk parameters, with a {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}-style stability module as the peg backstop. The architecture advertises collateral diversity, but the ledger tells a different story: roughly nine-tenths of the backing now sits in the stability module as frxUSD, with the isolated mint markets contributing only a thin tail of ETH, LST, and sUSDe debt, making it less a kitchen-sink CDP and more a Frax wrapper with an {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} garnish. That shows up in the classification: ALTO holders still govern the protocol, but the frxUSD dependency drags DUSD into centralized-dependent territory, inheriting Frax's {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} chain wholesale. The peg record is clean, with a top peg grade on a micro-cap float. The asset rarely strays from the calm end of the stress scale, though at this size calm owes as much to thin markets as to design. The solid report card with a slightly softer exit pillar sums it up: careful risk engineering. The biggest risk decision, the identity of the dollar backing yours, was settled in Frax's favor.

dusd-dtrinity.title: The Post-Exploit Bet on Frax
dusd-dtrinity.text: dUSD is dTRINITY's reserve-backed dollar with Curve AMOs; post-exploit trust rebuild on a Frax-heavy reserve. The March 17 exploit hit dTRINITY at the worst possible moment: a protocol with genuinely novel economics (subsidized borrowing funded by reserve {{term:yield-bearing}}yield{{/term}}) now carries a danger notice that overshadows everything else on the page. Supply has contracted to the low single-digit millions, Sonic deployment is paused, and the {{grade}} overall grade reflects failures in the backing pillar, where no current reserve composition is on file, and economic control. The reserve story tells the dependency tale: heavy sfrxUSD and Curve {{term:amo}}AMO{{/term}} positions mean dUSD is overwhelmingly a bet on Frax infrastructure, with chain-isolated reserves that at least prevent cross-chain contagion. Stress monitoring sits at the calm end of the scale, suggesting the acute crisis has stabilized, and the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop, which anchors the one pillar still earning a passing mark, is doing most of the peg-defense work. An elegant flywheel that proved fragile under pressure: the borrower subsidy model deserves a second chance, but this protocol needs to earn it.

sdusd-dtrinity.title: The dUSD Lender Receipt
sdusd-dtrinity.text: sdUSD is dTRINITY's yield-bearing wrapper for dUSD deposits in dLEND, so the token is best read as liquid dUSD lender exposure rather than a separate reserve asset. The wrapper is chain-isolated like dUSD itself: Ethereum sdUSD and Fraxtal sdUSD use separate deployments and are not fungible across chains. Yield comes from dLEND supply APY and accrues through the vault's NAV, while exits depend on available dUSD liquidity in dLEND or secondary-market depth. The important dependency is direct: sdUSD inherits dUSD reserve, peg, exploit, and dLEND bad-debt risk, with an extra strategy-vault layer on top. Pharos therefore treats sdUSD as a tracked {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} NAV variant of dUSD.

thbill-theo.title: Wrapping the Wrappers
thbill-theo.text: Theo's thBILL is a NAV-accreting T-bill wrapper whose reserve is currently tULTRA, itself a wrapped representation of Standard Chartered Libeara's ULTRA fund managed by Wellington. That means the holder gets institutional Treasury exposure, but only after passing through Theo, tULTRA, Libeara, Wellington, Standard Chartered custody, and the fund administration stack. Pharos gives the underlying collateral credit for being real T-bill exposure while still treating the wrapper depth and single-entity governance as operational risk, because a bond with four nameplates is still not direct bond ownership. Mint and redemption are KYC-gated, institutional, and not built for casual retail exit. Theo's own attention has visibly moved on. The last thBILL points market has ended and the issuer's incentives now push its new gold-carry product, leaving thBILL as inventory rather than flagship. thBILL is clean at the bottom and baroque at the top, which is apparently what tokenized Treasuries become when everyone wants their logo in the trust chain.

usdp-parallel.title: Parallelizer Basket Dollar
usdp-parallel.text: Parallel USDp is the liquid base dollar for a system built around the Parallelizer, a governed basket module rather than a single issuer bank account. The collateral list is a greatest-hits compilation of other stablecoin risks: frxUSD and sfrxUSD, USDe and sUSDe, USDS and sUSDS, plus USDC-linked Avalanche exposure. That makes the peg mechanics elegant and dependency analysis ugly, because overcollateralized basket issuance does not erase the fact that several upstream coins have their own governance, custody, and collateral assumptions. sPRL governance sets accepted collateral and exposure limits, so the real safety control is parameter discipline. USDp is useful as a liquid routing token, but it is a committee-managed index of other people's dollars rather than a clean dollar.

usdpt-western-union.title: Settlement Dollar, Now Spendable
usdpt-western-union.text: USDPT is Western Union's attempt to turn agent and treasury settlement into an on-chain dollar rail without pretending to be a DeFi-native coin. Anchorage Digital Bank issues it on Solana, with reserves in bank deposits and BlackRock's Treasury money-market fund, examined monthly by Deloitte under a regulated U.S. banking setup. The distribution thesis stopped being theoretical on August 4, 2026, when Western Union and stablecoin-payments firm Rain launched Stablecard, a USDPT wallet paired with a Visa card, live in 37 markets at launch. The product bolts consumer spend onto the physical agent network most issuers would pitch as a 2030 roadmap slide. Mint and redemption remain centralized issuer operations, and on-chain circulation has grown from four-figure dust at launch to pilot scale that is still a rounding error next to Western Union's remittance flows. In V9 terms that reads as strong backing behind a locked door: reserve quality grades near the top of the class while the exit pillar fails outright, because a holder's real exit is the issuer and the card, not the market. USDPT now extends beyond a settlement primitive. It has a storefront.

sources.label: crypto.news: Western Union launches USDPT Visa card with Rain

roughrider-bnd.title: State-Owned Banking Goes On-Chain
roughrider-bnd.text:
North Dakota's state-owned bank cleared its biggest hurdle on March 25 for a Solana-based bank-to-bank settlement coin, targeting September 2026.

North Dakota's Bank of North Dakota, the only state-owned bank in the US, cleared its biggest hurdle on March 25 when the Industrial Commission unanimously approved the bank-to-bank use case for Roughrider Coin. Ten local banks have already expressed pilot interest, CEO Don Morgan rates the risk as 'low to moderate,' and the project is expected to be cost-neutral to the state. The coin runs on Solana via Fiserv's infrastructure, backed by USD reserves and 93-day {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} notes under the GENIUS Act's state-issued stablecoin exemption. It won't be publicly tradeable. This is pure interbank settlement plumbing, voluntary for ND banks and credit unions. September 2026 remains the target, pending Fiserv contract finalization. As the second US state stablecoin after Wyoming's FRNT, Roughrider represents an emerging pattern: state treasurers discovering that blockchain settlement is cheaper than correspondent banking, even when the vote requires a closed-door executive session lasting two and a half hours.

fiusd-fiserv.title: The Payments Stack Play
fiusd-fiserv.text: FIUSD is Fiserv's pre-launch Solana dollar stablecoin built on Circle and Paxos infrastructure: a payments-rails play with four-partner coordination risk. Fiserv wants to make stablecoins just another rail in the infrastructure it already runs for roughly 10,000 financial institution clients and six million merchant locations, so FIUSD is less a single stablecoin and more a platform: Paxos handles issuance, Circle provides ecosystem interop, PayPal enables interoperability, and Mastercard connects the payments network. The centralized-dependent classification captures this architecture accurately; FIUSD depends on an entire constellation of {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} partners, any of which could become a {{term:bridge}}bottleneck{{/term}}. After the original end-of-2025 target slipped, CEO Mike Lyons said at June's Bernstein conference, "FIUSD goes live in July." July has now come and gone without a public launch confirmation, leaving Pharos still tracking the token as pre-launch. The interbank settlement pilot with Huntington and Bank of North Dakota remains the opening act, with the white-labeled Roughrider Coin queued behind it. The real test is whether four fintech giants can ship on one timeline.

sources.label: Payments Dive: Fiserv stablecoin arrives next month (June 3, 2026)
CoinDesk: Fiserv joins stablecoin fray with Circle, Paxos, PayPal (June 2025)

gelt-tether.title: Georgia's Lari, Tether's Rails
gelt-tether.text: GEL₮ is Tether's pre-launch Georgian Lari stablecoin, announced in May 2026 alongside the Government of Georgia and framed by Tether as the country's 'official' stablecoin. The framing is the story: a sovereign government handing its national currency's digital rails to the world's largest stablecoin issuer, while the National Bank of Georgia runs its own separate digital-lari pilot. The legal scaffolding is real. NBG Order No. 52/04 lets licensed issuers mint Lari-pegged tokens under 100% reserves, full redemption rights, and a GEL 500,000 capital floor, deliberately built for compatibility with the US GENIUS Act. Everything that matters for an assessment is still blank: no chains, no contracts, no reserve {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, no named {{term:custody}}custodian{{/term}}, no launch date. With prime-minister and central-bank endorsements but a non-USD peg Pharos doesn't yet price, this is a flag planted on a map rather than a token you can hold. Whether 'official' means anything more than a sharper logo on a 1:1 Tether liability is the question the missing disclosures will eventually answer.

eur-qivalis.title: Thirty-Seven Banks, One Euro
eur-qivalis.text: QEUR is a pre-launch MiCA-oriented euro stablecoin from a banking consortium that ballooned to 37 institutions across 15 countries by May 2026, up from 12 a few months earlier, targeting H2 2026 issuance under a Dutch EMI license. Qivalis is the European banking establishment's answer to USDC and Tether: a MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin now backed by names like BNP Paribas, ING, UniCredit, BBVA, ABN Amro, Intesa Sanpaolo, Rabobank, and Nordea. The reserve design uses 30-40% bank deposits and the remainder in short-term eurozone government bonds. It reads like a {{term:money-market-fund}}money market fund{{/term}} with a blockchain address. The chain question is settled: Ethereum mainnet first (ERC-20F with a permissioned KYC layer), then Polygon and Base. Only pre-verified participants can hold or transfer the token. This is the consortium's compromise between public-chain liquidity and institutional control. CEO Jan-Oliver Sell (ex-Coinbase Germany) is lining up exchange partnerships, and the EMI license application sits with De Nederlandsche Bank, filed but not granted; Qivalis says it will launch the moment approval lands. The central tension is unchanged and arguably sharper at 37 members: whether dozens of banks that compete fiercely everywhere else can cooperate long enough to ship before Circle's EURC and SocGen's EURCV finish eating the MiCA-compliant euro market. The ticker itself isn't even public yet. {{term:custody}}Custody{{/term}} sits across consortium banks and 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rights remain pre-launch commitments.

pusd-polaris.title: Immutable CDP, Yield Included
pusd-polaris.text:
A pre-launch Liquity-style immutable CDP stablecoin on Ethereum that captures protocol revenue for holders rather than reserve interest.

Polaris Finance is building what its co-founders TokenBrice and 0xLuude call the successor to Liquity's ethos: a crypto-collateralized stablecoin on Ethereum with immutable core contracts, no admin keys, and no off-chain assets. pUSD is minted against pETH collateral via {{term:cdp}}CDPs{{/term}}, and the {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} angle comes from protocol revenue: borrowing interest, swap fees, conversion gains, and DEX fees, rather than from depositing reserves into Aave. The private testnet is live with a Q4 2026 target, which gives the team time to prove that you can ship immutability without sacrificing usability. For a market saturated with centralized fiat-backed tokens and yield products built on leverage, pUSD is a deliberate bet that there's still demand for the Liquity V1 philosophy, upgraded.

pgold-polaris.title: Synthetic Gold, No Vault Required
pgold-polaris.text:
A pre-launch synthetic gold exposure minted from pETH via CDPs, with no physical backing. The design is decentralized but carries corresponding protocol risk.

Polaris Gold shares infrastructure with its sibling pUSD but pegs to gold rather than the dollar. It does so without any physical gold backing. Unlike XAUT or PAXG, which tokenize actual bars in Swiss vaults, pGOLD is a synthetic gold exposure minted from the same pETH collateral pool via {{term:cdp}}CDPs{{/term}} on Ethereum. This makes it arguably more decentralized than any gold-pegged token on the market, at the cost of carrying all the risks of crypto collateral in a down market. Whether DeFi users want synthetic gold exposure from immutable contracts instead of custodied metal from Tether or Paxos is an experiment Polaris is willing to run.

usg-tangent.title: Productive Collateral, Dynamic Rates
usg-tangent.text: Tangent Finance, which pivoted from the Convergence protocol after an August 2024 exploit, built USG as an {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin for productive DeFi collateral: Curve LP tokens, Pendle PTs, and other {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} or LP positions rather than plain ETH. The peg mechanism borrows from crvUSD's playbook but explicitly skips {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}: Peg Keepers, dynamic interest rates, and reward deductions grow more aggressive as USG weakens, pushing borrowers toward repayment while sUSG, the Yearn v3 savings wrapper, receives 25% of protocol revenue. Read the Etherscan supply line with care: roughly nine-tenths of the contract's total sits preminted in two protocol contracts, Peg Keeper-style, leaving genuine circulation in the low single-digit millions. There is still no CoinGecko or DefiLlama market row to price any of it. The v9 scorecard captures the beta candor precisely: a spotless peg record and mid-tier backing and exit pillars sit under an overall D, because economic control bottoms out at F on a multisig-run, centrally dependent system that lists five audit reports: Sherlock, Egis, two Pashov reviews, and Zerocool, beside placeholder site metrics. The design bets that DeFi-native collateral can be more capital-efficient than traditional {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} models, while inheriting the composability risk of every protocol whose tokens it accepts and a {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} surface only as deep as each underlying market.

klarnausd-klarna.title: KlarnaUSD testnet stablecoin on Tempo
klarnausd-klarna.text: Klarna's planned USD stablecoin runs on Tempo through Stripe Bridge Open Issuance, but it remains testnet-only with mainnet timing undecided. Klarna, the Swedish fintech with 114 million customers and $112B in annual GMV, is building the coin through Stripe's Bridge infrastructure on the Tempo L1. Tempo mainnet went live on March 18, 2026 with sub-second finality and fees under $0.001, and its Machine Payments Protocol, co-authored with Stripe, targets autonomous AI agent payments, yet KlarnaUSD was absent from a mainnet launch partners list that included Anthropic, Mastercard, Visa, and Revolut. The regulatory basis is firmer than the timeline: Bridge's conditional OCC national bank trust charter, approved in February, supplies regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and an {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} framework, while the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} window is scoped to Klarna's settlement flows rather than open DeFi liquidity. KlarnaUSD remains on Tempo's testnet, a matter of 'when' rather than 'if': Klarna's own payment volume is large enough to justify the infrastructure, and external adoption and DeFi liquidity are bonuses rather than requirements.

trusd-tori.title: Ethena's Playbook, Politely Executed
trusd-tori.text: trUSD is Tori Finance's run at the playbook Ethena popularized: a synthetic dollar backed by {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} trading positions ({{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} arbitrage, calendar spreads, hedged money markets) with a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} staked wrapper (strUSD), and the launch sequencing was unusually disciplined. Sherlock and Nethermind audits came before deployment, Accountable's real-time proof-of-solvency started on day one, and Nexus Mutual covered the pre-deposit vault. The $50M pre-deposit cap filled in seven days, and supply has kept growing past it, with a Curve trUSD-USDC pool now doing seven-figure daily volume as the main exit. What Pharos flagged as a controlled beta in May graduated to the active dashboard in August, which is the fastest rehabilitation arc in the upcoming tracker's short history. The open questions are the classic synthetic-dollar ones, and Pharos's on-chain review sharpened them: primary NAV mint/redeem is KYC-whitelisted in the contract itself (the 'no verification' marketing refers to secondary swaps), the custodian banks holding ~90% of attested backing are unnamed by policy, and independent tracing of the sole custodian wallet shows collateral flowing to exchange deposit addresses rather than anything resembling a bank. Delphi-backed, Ethereum-only, and single-entity operated: the peg has behaved so far, but this is a trading desk wearing a stablecoin's clothing, and the track record is measured in weeks.

ussd-sonic-labs.title: Yield Without the Yield
ussd-sonic-labs.text: Sonic Labs's USSD is a permissionless, zero-fee wrapper around Sonic frxUSD, so the reserve story belongs upstream to Frax rather than directly to a basket of {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} tokens. The design choice remains pointed: the {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} yield generated by that upstream backing flows to the Sonic ecosystem as buybacks and incentives, while USSD holders keep a flat dollar claim. That makes USSD less an independent stablecoin than a branded distribution layer over frxUSD, complete with the same reserve dependencies plus omnichain route risk of its own. If it reaches scale, the protocol captures the carry while users supply the non-yielding balance sheet. It is a tidy business model dressed as neutral infrastructure.

pgold-pleasing.title: Gold Without Receipts
pgold-pleasing.text:
Pleasing's gold token claims 1:1 physical bullion backing but publishes no proof of reserves or independent attestation, making it the least transparent gold token on the dashboard.

Pleasing Gold's PGOLD is backed 1:1 by LBMA-standard 99.99% physical gold at 1 troy ounce per token, deployed on Arbitrum and ApeChain. The same Pleasing International issues PUSD and shares the Hong Kong precious metals firm's physical gold corridor. The institutional-unregulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and absence of any proof of reserves or independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} make PGOLD the least transparent gold token on the dashboard, relying entirely on the issuer's claims without external verification. Whether a gold token without audited reserves can compete with PAXG's KPMG attestations and XAUT's BDO Italia audits depends on the holder's trust in the issuer rather than the metal itself. For Pleasing's existing gold corridor clients, PGOLD may serve as a convenient tokenized bridge; for everyone else, the lack of verifiable custody is a hard pass.

ggbr-goldfish-gold.title: The Paper Gold Token
ggbr-goldfish-gold.text: GGBR is Goldfish Gold's gold-tracking token at 1/1000 troy ounce per token, backed by issuer balance-sheet exposure rather than allocated bars, creating counterparty risk rather than custody risk. Goldfish Gold's GGBR represents 1/1000 of a troy ounce of gold per token, but unlike XAUT or PAXG, the backing is described as 'issuer balance-sheet gold exposure' rather than allocated physical bars, making it more a gold-tracking derivative than a tokenized commodity. The institutional-unregulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} with no published proof of reserves, no independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, and no disclosed jurisdiction means the entire trust chain runs through the Goldfish entity alone. Ethereum-only deployment with high-risk reserve classification reflects the Pharos assessment of what 'issuer-managed backing' means in practice: counterparty risk on the issuer rather than custody risk on the metal. In a tokenized gold market where PAXG offers individually serialized LBMA bars with KPMG attestations, GGBR's value proposition is hard to articulate beyond convenience.

gldt-gold-dao.title: NFT Gold, Fungible Wrapper
gldt-gold-dao.text: GLDT is Gold DAO's fungible wrapper over GLD NFTs, each token standing for a hundredth of a gram of Swiss-vaulted gold, and nothing about that structure changed this release. What changed is the date on the paperwork. Pharos had been dating the reserve composition to a mid-2026 read of the issuer's live page; opening the actual artefact re-anchored it to when the work was genuinely performed in September 2025. This puts it far outside the 31-day freshness window, drops the composition out of scoring entirely, and takes the backing pillar and the overall grade down to a D. The artefact repays the scrutiny: KPMG SA Neuchâtel signed a Swiss Auditing Standard 920 report of factual findings, expressly neither an audit nor a review and restricted in use, counting 7.9 kilograms of gold at a Loomis vault and reconciling it to GLD NFT certificates issued by Bity Tokenisation, not to GLDT supply. That series has not produced a successor in roughly ten and a half months. The gold is probably still in Kloten; what the record can no longer imply is that anyone checked recently, or that anyone ever checked against the token you actually hold.

axcnh-anchorx.title: The Offshore Yuan
axcnh-anchorx.text: AnchorX's AxCNH is a centralized offshore-yuan stablecoin backed by CNH cash reserves and issued under a Kazakhstan AFSA license. The product gives on-chain access to offshore Chinese yuan exposure, which is structurally interesting precisely because the onshore currency remains capital-controlled and politically delicate. Pharos now treats the custody model as institutional-regulated, but the trust stack is still almost entirely issuer-side: AnchorX manages minting, redemption, and reserve reporting, while Ethereum and Conflux mint surfaces depend on multisig-controlled issuer machinery. The reserve story is simple cash; the jurisdictional story is doing most of the work. AxCNH is less a DeFi primitive than a regulated corridor for a currency everyone wants near but not too near.

idrt-rupiah-token.title: Indonesia's Digital Rupiah
idrt-rupiah-token.text: Rupiah Token's IDRT is backed 1:1 by IDR bank deposits at PT Rupiah Token Indonesia and deployed natively across four chains, making it one of the more broadly distributed local-currency stablecoins. The proof story has inched forward: the issuer now publishes accountant-prepared AUP reports, a form of {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} that confirms bank balances without expressing assurance. {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} remains institutional and unregulated, and the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path still depends entirely on the issuer honoring KYC-gated fiat exits. The regulatory gray area is closing without IDRT in the room: OJK passed a rival rupiah-stablecoin issuer through its regulatory sandbox in June 2026, opening a formal registration path that turns self-defined compliance from a market condition into a choice. Pharos's report card is blunt: a failing overall grade with weak marks across backing, exit, and economic control. The peg holds only loosely, with dozens of recorded deviation events across a seven-year operating life. First-mover advantage in an unregulated market is worth a lot, right up until the regulator starts issuing hall passes to someone else.

sources.label: OJK June 2026 board meeting press release

tryb-bilira.title: The Lira's Digital Outpost
tryb-bilira.text: TRYB remains the most widely distributed on-chain lira, and the product itself has not changed: issuer-held TRY cash in Turkish bank accounts, centralized mint and redemption, and a use case that is obvious in a country where dollar rails dominate but local denomination still matters. What changed is a date. BiLira's reports come from Corpus Denetim as a genuine examination with full asset-and-liability reconciliation, materially better paperwork than most regional fiat tokens produce, but the examination covers a period ending in May, and Pharos now anchors composition to that examined date rather than the day the file appeared on the site. Outside the 31-day window the cash reserve stops counting, backing drops, and the grade falls to F on evidence timing rather than evidence quality. That is the uncomfortable arithmetic of a quarterly cycle: an honest examination goes stale between filings while a vaguer monthly self-report would not, and exit stays the other constraint, with no comparable same-notional route out of the position. TRYB is useful infrastructure with a disclosure-cadence problem, and that distinction matters most when the lira itself is doing lira things.

ebusd-ebisu.title: Exotic Collateral, Orderly Exit
ebusd-ebisu.text: Ebisu's ebUSD was a Liquity V2-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} with one of the most eclectic collateral baskets Pharos tracked: sUSDe, WBTC, LBTC, stcUSD, and weETH mixed into {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} branches deployed natively on Ethereum and Plasma. The mechanism was sound; the market never showed up. Supply peaked near $815K and had bled below $25K by the time the team announced a wind-down on July 29, 2026: minting paused, users asked to close Troves and pull Stability Pool and DEX deposits, and the frontend slated for deprecation at the end of October. The old editorial worry, that a micro-cap CDP is too small to attract the arbitrage that turns redemption into a real peg floor, turned out to be the entire story: fixed-rate credit at that scale could not generate enough borrowing to sustain the machine around it. Credit where due, collateral redemption stayed open throughout, making this that rarest of DeFi endings: solvent, orderly, and announced in advance.

usdaf-asymmetry.title: Immutable CDP, Recursive Collateral
usdaf-asymmetry.text: USDaf is an immutable Liquity V2 {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} minted from yield-bearing stablecoin and BTC collateral, structurally pure but still market-small. The collateral stack is recursive by design: ysyBOLD dominates, scrvUSD is material, sUSDS adds Sky exposure, and smaller tBTC, sfrxUSD, and WBTC slices round out the book. The live safety grade has improved from the old write-up, which is deserved for a system with immutable contracts, strong governance posture, and conservative {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}. The price of recursive decentralization remains steep: limited circulation, recurring depeg blips, and a market that does not always route sellers cleanly to the Liquity V2 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} floor. The permissionless collateral-redemption backstop is structurally sound and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} mechanics inherit Liquity's battle-tested design. USDaf is one of the purest expressions of trustless stablecoin design currently live; the recurring depeg blips price what that purity costs in market depth.

usnd-nerite.title: Immutable Code, Invisible Scale
usnd-nerite.text: Nerite's USND was a Liquity-V2 fork {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} dollar on Arbitrum, built on immutable contracts with permissionless collateral {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and, for a while, one of the cleanest decentralization-and-dependency profiles a nine-figure stablecoin could ask for. That profile is now academic: USND is frozen and carries an F across the board, the grade an archived asset earns once there is nothing left to score. The cause was structural rather than monetary. One approved collateral branch leaned on rsETH, and when the rsETH hack impaired it, immutable code meant Nerite could not patch the market away or rewrite the risk controls. Supply collapsed from a ~$2.7M peak to under $100K, and with such a thin exit door, the {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} machinery had no scale left to defend the peg. DEWS still sits at the calm end of the stress scale, but that reading reflects the frozen, inactive market rather than a healthy peg. USND was the answer to a question very few people were asking: whether you can build a truly decentralized, immutable stablecoin that scores well on every metric except the one that requires other people to care. The rsETH hack settled it: contracts nobody could amend had no way to shed the impaired branch, and what remains is under $100K of frozen supply.

ftusd-flying-tulip.title: On-Chain Carry, Concentrated Control
ftusd-flying-tulip.text: ftUSD is Flying Tulip's non-yielding base dollar, while sftUSD is the optional wrapper that receives strategy yield. The live reserve stack lends stablecoin collateral and runs borrow-and-stake carry on both Ethereum and Sonic: WETH into wstETH exposure on Ethereum and wS into stS on Sonic, not a short-perpetual hedge. Flying Tulip's token-sale capital is not conventional operating runway: primary FT allocations carry a perpetual put against reserved contributed assets, and the issuer says operations are funded from generated yield and revenue. Yield attributable to unstaked ftUSD accrues to the protocol, an opportunity-cost transfer distinct from a mandatory yield-bearing token. Flying Tulip indexes the reserve feed, while the underlying balances are publicly verifiable on-chain. The remaining risks include lending and staking/liquidation exposure, upstream USDC/USDT/USSD dependencies, and the same no-timelock 3-of-5 Safe controlling token ownership, master-minter authority, and the upgradeable minter on both chains.

brla-brla-digital.title: Brazil's Dollar Problem, Inverted
brla-brla-digital.text: BRLA is Avenia's centralized Brazilian real stablecoin, minted and redeemed 1:1 for BRL and backed by Brazilian government bonds and BRL cash in regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, inverting the usual emerging-market dollar-escape pattern. Most stablecoins help users leave a local currency for dollars; BRLA tokenizes the real for on-chain settlement instead. Its native footprint spans several non-Ethereum networks, while upgrade and compliance roles leave blacklisting and contract control with a single operator rather than a DAO. The reserve story is still issuer-led, so the useful multichain distribution comes with a familiar centralized question: how much confidence should a tokenized real borrow from the entity holding the real assets? Yield variants position BRLA as BRL-denominated DeFi infrastructure, but the trust model remains considerably more traditional than the rails.

silk-shade-protocol.title: The Vault Nobody Can Liquidate
silk-shade-protocol.text: SILK is still the most conceptually ambitious basket stablecoin on Pharos: a GDP-weighted index of twenty currencies, defended by {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} vaults, running natively on Secret Network's privacy chain. It is also, on inspection, a nineteen-vault lending book priced through a single oracle provider with no failover and an empty deviation-guard list. The finding that matters sits in the WBTC vault, second-largest at 18.3% of ShadeLend's elastic debt: it is governance-frozen against roughly 37.9k SILK of debt backed by about 0.00002 WBTC, its {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} query reverts on a divide-by-zero, and its collateral staleness tolerance has been widened from the 600 seconds every other vault uses to a number with fourteen digits. The check is off. Two more collateral oracles have been rejecting queries as stale since February 2025 and July 2026 respectively, and the Stability Pool holds well under half the protocol's aggregate debt with no documented socialization path for a shortfall. A basket that hedges twenty currencies is an elegant answer to a question nobody was asking; a stranded vault with the staleness check disabled is a plainer problem.

idrx-idrx.title: Rupiah Rails With Audit Claims
idrx-idrx.text: IDRX is a rupiah stablecoin with a reserve story that at least knows what country it is in: IDR fiat reserves and Indonesian government bonds, backed by issuer-published transparency and audit materials. The KYC-gated mint and redemption flow makes it more like regulated local payment infrastructure than a free-floating DeFi primitive. Native multichain deployment expands reach, but Pharos still records a centralized issuer model with EOA-admin upgrade authority and minter controls that deserve more than a shrug. The proof path is stronger than a self-reported spreadsheet, yet it remains an issuer-controlled local-currency coin in a market where liquidity can vanish faster than compliance paperwork. IDRX is credible enough to be interesting and centralized enough to remain easy to grade with a raised eyebrow.

mxnb-juno.title: Peso Stablecoin, New Issuer Jurisdiction
mxnb-juno.text: 1:1 MXN-pegged stablecoin with quarterly attestations; issuer just moved from Mexico (CNBV) to El Salvador (CNAD) as of April 2026, with reserves still in regulated peso banking. MXNB remains a 1:1 Mexican peso stablecoin with quarterly reserve {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} and the same multichain FiatToken-style deployment across Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, and Avalanche. The material change is issuer jurisdiction: beginning April 8, 2026, MXNB says issuance moved to Nvio Pagos El Salvador, S.A. de C.V., an authorised digital-asset issuer in El Salvador. The reserves are still described as Mexican peso assets held with regulated financial institutions under bank {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, so Pharos keeps the fiat-backed model while updating the regulatory owner from Mexico/CNBV to El Salvador/CNAD. Distribution took an institutional turn in June with MXNB joining XRP Ledger's permissioned DEX paired against RLUSD for cross-border USD/MXN settlement. This corridor infrastructure is exactly the job a peso stablecoin should want.

cjpy-yamato.title: ETH-Backed Yen, Quietly Running
cjpy-yamato.text: CJPY is Yamato's decentralized JPY stablecoin from ETH-only {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}s, built by DeFiGeek Community Japan without a corporate issuer. The mechanism echoes Liquity's playbook: deposit ETH at 130% minimum collateralization, borrow CJPY with a one-time fee and no accruing interest, and use accumulated protocol fees to absorb underwater positions. Its {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route lets CJPY return one yen worth of ETH from the riskiest pledge, giving the peg an on-chain floor without a bank account or blacklist operator. Ethereum-only deployment and a niche circulation keep it philosophically closer to RAI and LUSD than to the centralized yen issuers dominating the category. The purity is real; so is the possibility that a clean design remains a specialist instrument rather than a liquid currency.

usdkg-gold-dollar.title: Kyrgyz Gold, Dollar Wrapper
usdkg-gold-dollar.text: USDKG is a Kyrgyz Republic gold-backed stablecoin minted against 376 kg of LBMA bullion, with 100.6% overcollateralization but only ISRS 4400 procedures rather than a full audit {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. USDKG is a sovereign experiment in commodity-backed stablecoin design: the Kyrgyz Republic's Ministry of Finance sold 376 kilograms of LBMA Good Delivery gold bars to LLC Virelint Group, which stores them in sealed boxes at an unnamed bank, and the state-owned OJSC "Issuer of Virtual Assets" mints USD-pegged tokens against that pile. The gold is real. Kyrgyzaltyn, the state mining monopoly that refined it, has been LBMA-listed since 2022. The trust chain from bullion to token runs through private intermediaries whose bank won't even let auditors see the access logs. Kreston Global's quarterly report is an ISRS 4400 agreed-upon procedures engagement, not an audit, and it explicitly disclaims assurance. That distinction matters when 100.6% overcollateralization is the only buffer between a gold price dip and undercollateralization. The ConsenSys Diligence smart contract audit found no critical issues but confirmed what the architecture implies: owner multisig can pause all transfers, compliance multisig can blacklist any address and destroy its tokens. At $50M across Tron and Ethereum with thin DEX-only liquidity, USDKG is less a stablecoin for DeFi and more a cross-border payments rail for Central Asian corridors. Confidence in Bishkek's gold vaults must match the confidence inspired by Brink's London.

usdh-hermetica.title: Bitcoin's Synthetic Dollar, On Stacks
usdh-hermetica.text: Hermetica's USDh is the Ethena playbook on Bitcoin-native infrastructure: a {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar deployed on Stacks L2 with a Runes variant on Bitcoin L1. BTC spot plus short {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} futures create the offsetting exposure, and the product is unusual for touching neither Ethereum nor an EVM chain. Yield flows to sUSDh stakers via {{term:funding-rate}}funding-rate{{/term}} payments from the short perpetual positions, so returns depend on funding staying favorable rather than on the size of Hermetica's seed round. Minting requires KYC/AML verification through Hermetica's app, collateral sits on centralized exchanges with CEX-tier {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and a DIA oracle prices the token on-chain. This trust stack makes the asset less a trustless Bitcoin dollar and more a managed fund with a Clarity smart contract wrapper. The single-chain, single-entity design is refreshingly honest about what it is: a bet that Bitcoin's basis trade can sustain a stablecoin ecosystem outside the EVM monoculture.

usdsc-startale.title: Sony's Dollar, M0's Plumbing
usdsc-startale.text: USDSC is a Soneium-exclusive 1:1 wrapper around M0's M, carrying the same short-term {{term:treasury}}Treasury-bill backing{{/term}}, Validator {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, and bankruptcy-remote SPV structure into Startale's app ecosystem. It is less a fresh reserve design than a distribution wager: give Sony's L2 a branded dollar, add freeze authority and local integrations, and hope chain gravity supplies the demand. The wrapper inherits M0's backing quality while adding Startale's operator and single-chain dependencies, a reminder that institutional plumbing can still acquire a new control surface at every layer. Whether Soneium needs its own M0 wrapper is unresolved; the lineage is credible, but logos are easier to multiply than liquidity.

ctusd-citrea.title: Bitcoin's Dollar, MoonPay's Rails
ctusd-citrea.text: ctUSD is Citrea's native dollar issued by MoonPay on M0, backed by T-bill assets with a broad fiat on-ramp, but still small on a young Bitcoin ZK-rollup. The infrastructure is standard M0: bankruptcy-remote SPVs, on-chain Validator {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, short-term {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} backing: the same infrastructure that now underwrites a growing family of branded dollars across the ecosystem. Circulation has multiplied several-fold since the January launch yet remains in the single-digit millions on a single chain, so the value proposition is still distribution over destination: MoonPay's 30 million-plus verified users can buy in via Visa, Mastercard, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and PayPal across 49 U.S. states and 160-plus countries, an on-ramp far wider than the destination chain's current user base. Founders Fund and Galaxy sit on Citrea's cap table, lending the institutional credibility that typically accompanies products ten times this size. The report card catches the real tension: a spotless peg and solid economic control dragged to a C- by middling backing evidence and an exit pillar graded D; reserves are an {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} short-Treasury fund, but {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs back through MoonPay's fiat rails or a DEX market that barely exists. The bet remains that Bitcoin needs a native, compliant dollar more than this dollar has yet needed Bitcoin.

sources.label: Citrea: Introducing ctUSD (MoonPay user base, payment rails, coverage, backers)

usdat-saturn.title: Saylor's Yield, M0's Backing
usdat-saturn.text: Saturn's USDat is a permissioned M0 wrapper of short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} in a bankrupt-remote SPV.
