Itau Unibanco, Brazil's largest private bank by assets, confirmed in April 2025 that it is evaluating its own stablecoin, with Head of Digital Assets Guto Antunes telling a Sao Paulo industry event the bank is 'always open to understanding whether it makes sense for our clients to have a stablecoin, even one in real, within Itau'. The peg-currency choice (BRL or USD) is explicitly undecided and gated on the final shape of Brazil's regulatory framework via BCB Consulta Publica 111, especially the open self-{{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} question that Antunes flagged as a major design constraint. Itau already participates in the DREX wholesale CBDC pilot, providing distribution-rail experience but also a competing institutional product that may shape final positioning; primary {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} would presumably run through Itau's bank network. The placeholder is BRL-denominated because Brazil's retail base and Itau's franchise make a real-denominated launch the most likely first design, while Itau has not ruled out a USD-denominated option.

moveusd-cfx.title: CFX's Solana Deposit Dollar
moveusd-cfx.text: CFX-issued tokenized-deposit dollar on Solana, roughly $120M circulating against USD deposits, cash equivalents, and U.S. Treasuries; no independent reserve feed is public yet. MoveUSD is a CFX-issued dollar settlement instrument with DefiLlama reporting roughly $120M in circulating supply and a live Solana price path. The token is best read as tokenized-deposit infrastructure rather than a permissionless DeFi-native stablecoin: minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} run through the issuer, while the SPL mint gives Pharos a concrete on-chain supply anchor. Reserves are described as USD deposits, cash equivalents, and marketable U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} securities, but no independently audited reserve feed is public yet. The detail page carries a tokenized-deposit caveat so users do not confuse the high market cap with open retail redemption coverage.

hlusd-hela.title: HeLa's Native Runtime Dollar
hlusd-hela.text: Centralized USD stablecoin for the HeLa chain; CoinGecko-only coverage, no contract-level reserve telemetry yet. HLUSD is the native dollar stablecoin for the HeLa ecosystem, admitted through CoinGecko because the HeLa chain is not yet a supported Pharos contract platform. CoinGecko reports a positive price and market cap, but contract-level supply and issuer reserve telemetry remain outside the supported chain set. The asset is therefore classified as a centralized-dependent RWA-backed USD coin with an explicit unsupported-chain notice. The unusually high trading volume relative to supply makes it useful coverage, while HeLa chain support and stronger reserve documentation remain the main open data gaps. Until the issuer publishes a verifiable {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} and discloses {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path remains the dominant unknown.

xmd-metal-dollar.title: A Stablecoin Basket on XPR Network
xmd-metal-dollar.text:
Metallicus's basket dollar wraps USDC, PYUSD, and Paxos-dollar exposure on XPR Network. The structure is convenient as an index but hard to verify outside CoinGecko.

Metal Dollar is a basket-backed dollar token on XPR Network, with public materials pointing to USDC, PYUSD, and Paxos-dollar components as the reserve set held in issuer {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. Pharos admits it through CoinGecko's price and market-cap path because XPR Network is not currently supported for contract coverage. The structure gives XMD upstream exposure to centralized stablecoin issuers while leaving direct holder-control semantics hard to verify from Pharos' chain set, and no public {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} feed itemizes the basket weights. It is useful basket-stablecoin coverage, but Pharos keeps dependency weights coarse until reserve composition and redemption depth are disclosed more granularly.

vusd-virtue.title: IOTA-Backed CDP Dollar
vusd-virtue.text: Virtue USD is an IOTA-ecosystem {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin backed by IOTA and stIOTA positions, with high-risk collateral and IOTA not yet a Pharos-supported chain. Virtue USD is an {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} IOTA ecosystem stablecoin backed by IOTA and stIOTA positions, with {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} as peg defense. CoinGecko resolves the IOTA object and reports a positive market cap, but IOTA itself is not yet a Pharos-supported chain, so the registry currently excludes contracts. That means Pharos can show price, market-cap, and risk metadata, while on-chain supply, mint/burn, and contract authority analysis remain future work. The collateral profile is high-risk compared with fiat-backed stablecoins because peg defense ultimately depends on volatile IOTA-family collateral and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} mechanics.

stusd-stoneyield.title: A Yield Wrapper Wearing a Dollar Label
stusd-stoneyield.text: StoneYield USD is a BNB Chain yield wrapper over USDC and Venus-linked strategy positions, not a plain fiat dollar with a bank account behind it. The reserve model points to USDC routed through StoneYield's managed protocol layer, so stability depends on both the underlying stablecoin and the strategy wrapper doing what it says on the label. Pharos marks stUSD as yield-bearing and NAV-style because the holder is accepting vault mechanics, admin controls, and withdrawal liquidity risk in exchange for the yield path. CoinGecko can provide the market row, but a stronger independent APY and reserve feed would make the entry less dependent on issuer-side framing. It is a dollar wrapper in the same way a structured note is cash: close enough for marketing, not close enough for risk.

lvusd-leverup.title: Monad Perps Collateral in Stablecoin Form
lvusd-leverup.text: Small Monad-based stable asset tied to LeverUp's perpetuals engine, not a cash-backed issuer dollar; redemption and reserve depth depend on a trading system rather than a bank balance sheet. LeverUp USD is a small Monad stablecoin tied to LeverUp's liquidity layer for perpetuals and margin trading. CoinGecko reports a live price and market cap, and the Monad contract is included because Pharos already has a Monad chain entry. The risk profile is not comparable to a cash-backed issuer coin: collateral and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} are tied to a trading engine that references USDC and MON, and public reserve depth is still thin. Pharos therefore treats lvUSD as a notice-heavy crypto-backed stable asset rather than a conventional dollar reserve token.

nusd-nexus.title: Legacy Synapse Bridge Liquidity
nusd-nexus.text: Legacy Synapse bridge-liquidity stable asset backed by a DAI/USDC/USDT pool; closer to bridge routing infrastructure than a standalone modern issuer, with inherited freezability and dependency risk. Nexus USD is a legacy Synapse {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}}-liquidity stable asset backed by a pool of DAI, USDC, and USDT. It is included because DefiLlama still returns both a current price and circulating supply, but the product model is closer to bridge routing infrastructure than to a standalone modern issuer. The upstream reserve basket gives NUSD inherited freezability and stablecoin dependency risk. Contract coverage is intentionally omitted until the active Synapse deployment set is freshly verified across chains.

brlm-mento.title: Mento's Brazilian Real Rail
brlm-mento.text: BRLm is Mento's oracle-priced Brazilian real on Celo, exchanged through FPMM swap routes against the diversified {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} Mento reserve mix. BRLm expands Mento coverage into Brazilian real-denominated settlement on Celo. Unlike the existing Mento {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} rows, this entry uses the reserve-wide Mento dashboard feed because the current CDP trove API only covers GBPm, JPYm, and CHFm. The reserve mix is diversified but still exposed to sUSDS, CELO, EURC, USDC, USDT, axlEUROC, stETH, and smaller assets, so Pharos classifies collateral quality as mixed rather than fiat-reserve grade. BRLm is small in absolute supply, but strategically useful because it adds another BRL rail from an already-modeled issuer family.

phpm-mento.title: The Unpriceable Peso
phpm-mento.text: PHPm, Mento's Celo-native Philippine peso token originally marketed as PUSO, is no longer actively tracked: Pharos terminated coverage in July 2026 after the token proved unpriceable by dashboard standards, its only accepted price path being an exact Mento Broker route with fail-closed guardrails that could not sustain reliable coverage. The mechanism was never a PHP bank account: under Mento V3, the non-dollar FX stables are minted CDP-style against USDm through a Liquity-v2 fork, so the peso peg rested on oracle pricing with a dollar stablecoin as collateral. Rather than lean on thin Celo DEX pools to conjure a quote, the pricing pipeline preferred an explicit coverage gap. The fail-closed posture does exactly what it was designed to do. Should Mento's Broker route regain sustained depth, the listing case reopens; until then, PHPm exists on Celo but not on this dashboard. A peso peg nobody can reliably price is a proposition, not a product.

kesm-mento.title: First Kenyan Shilling Stablecoin Coverage
kesm-mento.text: First Kenyan shilling stable in Pharos; runs on Celo via Mento's reserve-backed FX mechanism, grouped under OTHER until KES has a dedicated peg category. KESm is the first Kenyan shilling-denominated stable asset in Pharos, admitted through DefiLlama's price and circulating-supply path. The token runs on Celo and uses the same Mento reserve-backed FX mechanism as the newer Mento local-currency suite. Because KES does not yet have a dedicated Pharos peg category, the asset is grouped under OTHER. The reserve risk remains driven by the Mento mix, especially CELO exposure and upstream centralized stablecoins. Mechanically KESm is a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style Mento FX stablecoin with {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} against the multi-asset reserve and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} via FPMM swaps at oracle-driven rates.

copm-mento.title: Colombian Peso Coverage via Celo
copm-mento.text: COPm is Mento's oracle-priced Colombian peso stablecoin on Celo; first COP reference on Pharos. COPm adds Colombian peso stablecoin coverage through Mento's Celo deployment. DefiLlama supplies price and circulating-value data, while the contract is verified from the Celo token-contract table. COP is grouped under OTHER rather than a dedicated peg category. The addition is small-cap but useful because it gives the dashboard a first Colombian peso reference. The reserve relies on {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} across a mixed crypto and stablecoin basket and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through Mento reserve swaps.

cadm-mento.title: A Tiny CAD Rail from Mento
cadm-mento.text: CADm is Mento's oracle-priced CAD stablecoin on Celo, backed by the shared Mento reserve rather than Canadian bank reserves. CADm is Mento's Canadian dollar stable asset on Celo, added mainly for ecosystem completion rather than market size. DefiLlama provides price and supply coverage, and the token uses a verified Celo contract, but circulating supply remains tiny compared with larger CAD stablecoin issuers already tracked by Pharos. The collateral story is Mento reserve exposure rather than Canadian-dollar bank reserves. That means resilience depends on Celo, Mento governance, and the mixed reserve basket behind the broader Mento system. The reserve relies on {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} across a basket of stablecoins and crypto, and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through Mento reserve swaps rather than fiat off-ramps.

audm-mento.title: Mento's AUD Completes Another Local Rail
audm-mento.text: AUDm is Mento's crypto-backed Australian dollar on Celo, minted by depositing USDm as Liquity-v2-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} collateral against the {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} Mento reserve mix. AUDm is the Mento Australian dollar asset on Celo, distinct from the already tracked Macropod AUDM despite the shared ticker style. It is admitted through DefiLlama and a verified Celo contract, with live reserve visibility through the shared Mento dashboard. The supply is small, so the value is mainly comparative: users can now see Mento's AUD rail beside larger AUD issuers and the rest of the Mento FX set. Reserves remain mixed and on-chain rather than an Australian-dollar banking stack.

ghsm-mento.title: Ghanaian Cedi Coverage, Grouped as Other
ghsm-mento.text: GHSm is Mento's Celo Ghanaian cedi stablecoin backed by a mixed reserve (sUSDS, CELO, EURC, USDC, stETH). It provides small-supply currency coverage rather than a market signal. GHSm brings Ghanaian cedi exposure into Pharos through Mento's Celo stablecoin suite. DefiLlama provides price and supply data, while CoinGecko's active slug resolves as cGHS rather than the stale DefiLlama gecko hint. Like KESm and COPm, GHSm is grouped under OTHER because GHS does not yet have a dedicated peg category. It is very small, but it extends coverage into a currency region otherwise missing from the dashboard, with backing tied to Mento's shared {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} reserve and on-chain {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} flows.

zarm-mento.title: Mento's Smaller ZAR Stablecoin
zarm-mento.text:
Celo-issued ZAR stable from Mento's local-currency program, inheriting reserve risk from the shared Mento mix rather than ZAR bank collateral.

ZARm is a Celo-based South African rand stable asset from Mento minted {{term:cdp}}CDP-style{{/term}} against the Mento Reserve mix. Pharos already tracks a larger ZAR issuer, so ZARm is mainly an ecosystem-completion row that lets users compare Mento's local-currency model across regions. The token passes the DefiLlama price and supply gate and uses the verified Celo contract. Reserve quality is inherited from the shared Mento reserve mix rather than from rand-denominated bank collateral, so {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} risk is on the Mento basket, not the South African banking system.

wbrl-ripio.title: Ripio's Wrapped Brazilian Real
wbrl-ripio.text: WBRL is Ripio's wrapped Brazilian real stablecoin across six EVM chains. It is a second BRL rail from a Latin American issuer, with reserve transparency as the weak point. WBRL is part of Ripio's wFIAT suite: local-currency stablecoins issued across Ethereum, Base, World Chain, BNB Chain, Polygon, and Gnosis. It passes DefiLlama's price and circulating-supply gate and gives Pharos a second BRL rail from a Latin American issuer, alongside larger BRL assets already tracked. The contract address is consistent across supported EVM chains via {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} infrastructure, simplifying token discovery. The weak point is reserve transparency: Ripio describes local-currency {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} backing and a {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path, but no reliable per-token WBRL attestation is currently public.

wclp-ripio.title: First Chilean Peso Runtime Row
wclp-ripio.text: WCLP is Ripio's wrapped Chilean peso token and gives Pharos active CLP exposure even though the peg still sits under the broader OTHER bucket. The product is issuer-managed local-currency infrastructure: Chilean-peso cash and liquid instruments behind a 1 WCLP = 1 CLP target, deployed across the same EVM footprint Ripio uses for its wFIAT suite. The useful part is runtime coverage through DefiLlama price and circulating value plus consistent contract addresses across supported chains. The weak part is reserve transparency, because public materials describe custody and redemption in broad terms without a reliable per-token attestation feed. WCLP expands the map, but it does not yet make the reserve evidence any less local and issuer-shaped.

wcop-ripio.title: Ripio's Colombian Peso wFIAT Token
wcop-ripio.text: WCOP is Ripio's Colombian peso wFIAT token with off-chain local-currency backing and multi-chain EVM issuance, overlapping with Mento COPm but using a different issuer model. WCOP is the Ripio wFIAT Colombian peso token, added through DefiLlama's price and supply coverage with verified supported-chain deployments. It overlaps thematically with Mento COPm but uses a different issuer model: off-chain local-currency {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} backing and multi-chain EVM issuance via {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} infrastructure rather than Celo's Mento reserve. COP is still grouped under OTHER pending broader peg-currency support. The main open gap is reserve evidence, since Ripio's public page does not provide a reliable per-token WCOP attestation or detailed {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} terms.

wpen-ripio.title: Peruvian Sol Coverage from Ripio
wpen-ripio.text: Ripio's PEN-pegged wrapper extends Latam fiat coverage across six EVM chains, but per-token reserve attestation is missing. WPEN adds Peruvian sol exposure to Pharos through Ripio's local-currency stablecoin suite. DefiLlama supplies price and circulating-supply data, and Ripio's same-address EVM deployment pattern lets Pharos track contracts on Ethereum, Base, World Chain, BNB Chain, Polygon, and Gnosis via {{term:bridge}}bridged{{/term}} routes. PEN is grouped under OTHER because it does not yet have a dedicated peg category. Like the rest of the new Ripio rows, reserve transparency is the limiting factor: the backing model is described under issuer {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, but no per-token {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} feed is public enough to verify {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} capacity.

jaaa-janus-henderson-anemoy.title: AAA CLO Exposure as a Tokenized Fund
jaaa-janus-henderson-anemoy.text: NAV-accreting AAA CLO fund share via Anemoy/Centrifuge; permissioned, KYC-gated, not a $1 redeemable stablecoin. JAAA is not a dollar redeemable stablecoin in the usual sense: it is a NAV-accreting Janus Henderson AAA CLO fund share issued through Anemoy and Centrifuge rails. Pharos treats the Chainlink NAV feed as live reserve evidence, while the reserve-risk model stays conservative because even AAA CLO tranches are structured credit rather than cash or Treasury bills. The token has multi-chain contract coverage, but primary-market access remains permissioned and KYC-gated. Institutional support keeps thickening around it. Kraken added JAAA to qualified custody and Ethena's risk committee approved it as an eligible reserve asset, pulling a permissioned CLO share ever deeper into stablecoin collateral stacks. The fund share is {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} structured-credit {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}, with Centrifuge {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and permissioned {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at NAV rather than open par exit.

acrdx-anemoy-apollo.title: Apollo Credit Through Anemoy
acrdx-anemoy-apollo.text: ACRDX is a permissioned, NAV-accreting share token from Anemoy and Centrifuge giving on-chain access to Apollo's diversified private credit strategy, not a par stablecoin or cash-like asset. ACRDX packages Apollo Diversified Credit Fund exposure into an Anemoy tokenized share class. The backing spans private corporate direct lending, asset-backed lending, performing credit, and opportunistic credit sleeves, so Pharos classifies the reserves as high-risk {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} credit rather than cash-like collateral. Chronicle proof-of-asset coverage provides useful NAV visibility, but {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} remains a permissioned fund process.

stac-securitize.title: CLO Fund Access on Securitize
stac-securitize.text: STAC is a Securitize-issued tokenized fund share for a BNY-advised AAA CLO portfolio, which makes it dollar-denominated without making it a dollar. The token is priced by fund NAV and investor access runs through Securitize's qualification, transfer-control, and primary-market process, so there is no open $1 redemption backstop hiding behind the ticker. Chronicle proof-of-asset coverage improves transparency around the fund exposure, but Pharos still treats the collateral as high-risk structured credit rather than cash-like reserves. The exit pillar carries an F even as backing and economic control fare respectably. The distribution story has broadened: the fund expanded to Solana in June with Ethena committing $250 million, one of the larger tokenized-credit allocations on that chain, and issuer Securitize is now a public company. Its Cantor SPAC merger closed in early July and the stock trades on the NYSE as SECZ after raising roughly $400 million. The funny part is that AAA appears in the fund name while the stablecoin dashboard still has to ask the rude question: can you actually exit when you need to?

sources.label: Securitize expands STAC to Solana with $250M Ethena allocation (PRNewswire, 2026-06-12)
Securitize lists on NYSE as SECZ as $400M SPAC deal closes (Bitcoin.com News)

hlscope-hamilton-lane.title: Hamilton Lane Private Credit Rail
hlscope-hamilton-lane.text: Tokenized senior secured private-credit fund priced at NAV; primary access permissioned, not an open-redemption $1 stablecoin. HLSCOPE tokenizes Hamilton Lane Senior Credit Opportunities Fund exposure through Securitize. The asset belongs in the NAV-token cohort: price follows fund NAV, while subscriptions and redemptions are handled through permissioned fund infrastructure rather than open stablecoin liquidity. Reserve risk is high because the backing is private credit, not short-term cash instruments. Distribution keeps stretching. A June TRON deployment via Wormhole made HLSCOPE the first Securitize-issued asset on that chain, an odd-couple pairing of private credit and payments rails. This is an {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} fund share rather than a par dollar. Subscriptions and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} run through Securitize's permissioned {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} rail at NAV.

pc0000031-tradable.title: Private Credit Note, Not a Liquid Dollar
pc0000031-tradable.text: Yield-bearing private-credit note with CoinGecko price and market-cap coverage but no public APY or cashflow feed; intentionally kept out of live yield rankings, no redemption backstop assigned. Tradable PC0000031 is tracked as a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} private-credit note ({{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} exposure) with CoinGecko price and market-cap coverage, but no reliable public APY or cashflow feed is available. It remains outside live yield rankings because no reliable public APY or cashflow feed is available, and no {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop is assigned because there is no public primary redemption route comparable to issuer stablecoin redemption.

pc0000033-tradable.title: Par Value, Private Credit
pc0000033-tradable.text: PC0000033 is a Tradable senior secured term-note token backed by APAC consumer-financing receivables, including line-of-credit and BNPL exposure. It is contract-priced at note par, not defended by a liquid secondary-market peg, so calling it a $1 stablecoin would be doing the word stablecoin a small accounting crime. Pharos admits it through runtime market-price and supply coverage while keeping the reserve slice high-risk and the issuer dependence explicit. Minting is permissioned through Tradable's zkSync deal machinery, and the public yield source is still missing rather than politely hallucinated. The token is useful as private-credit infrastructure; it is not a cash substitute unless your cash desk is unusually fond of term-note servicing risk.

pc0000101-tradable.title: Legal Finance at Par
pc0000101-tradable.text: PC0000101 is Tradable's tokenized exposure to a Victory Park senior post-settlement legal-financing facility for a U.S. law firm. The token is priced at $1 note par by contract and issuer servicing, not by a liquid market defending a payment-stablecoin peg. Pharos therefore treats the CoinGecko price as a private-credit reference point and flags the zero-volume reality instead of pretending there is deep exit liquidity. The reserve is a single high-risk legal-finance receivables slice, minted only through Tradable's permissioned zkSync issuance path. This is a securitized receivable wearing dollar notation, which is useful if you want that risk and deeply misleading if you wanted cash.

pc0000089-tradable.title: Residential Credit, Tokenized
pc0000089-tradable.text: PC0000089 is a Tradable token for a Latin American residential-lending senior secured term-loan note, issued through Victory Park and represented on zkSync. The $1 reference is contract par, not a market-cleared stablecoin peg, and Pharos keeps that distinction visible because private credit does not become cash by wearing two decimal places. The collateral is a single high-risk LatAm residential credit exposure with centralized issuer controls and permissioned minting by Tradable's issuance EOA. A live price and market cap make the token trackable; zero-volume warnings and no public yield row keep the dashboard from overselling liquidity or income transparency. It is a credit note first, an on-chain asset second, and a stablecoin only in the loosest possible dinner-party taxonomy.

asusdf-astherus.title: Astherus Yield Wrapper
asusdf-astherus.text: asUSDF is Aster's staked wrapper over USDF, so the wrapper share accrues yield while the base stablecoin risk remains USDF's Ceffu, Binance, and MirrorX strategy stack. Deposits mint asUSDF against USDF, and exits return USDF only after Aster's documented waiting period, which is not quite the same thing as instant dollar liquidity no matter how smooth the UI feels. Pharos captures the reserve dependency as 100% wrapped USDF rather than pretending the wrapper has an independent balance sheet. The extra yield comes from delta-neutral and funding-fee strategies upstream, meaning asUSDF is best read as USDF plus queue risk, role-controlled wrapper minting, and a little more patience demanded from anyone leaving.

mf-one-midas.title: Fasanara F-ONE tokenized strategy certificate
mf-one-midas.text: mF-ONE is a Midas tokenized certificate over Fasanara's F-ONE strategy, spanning fintech receivables, SME lending, real-estate-backed credit, and digital-asset strategies. That makes it a permissioned NAV product, not a bank-reserve stablecoin, and the daily price story comes from strategy valuation rather than a hard $1 redemption floor. Pharos gives it a live valuation route through the Midas transparency setup, while still marking the collateral as high-risk because private credit plus digital-asset strategy exposure is not the conservative end of the menu. Issuance and redemption run through Midas rails, with upgrades and admin rights concentrated behind the Midas control stack. The product is sophisticated, but its centralization and portfolio opacity remain material constraints. Those constraints matter more than the strategy's packaging when assessing the token's NAV exposure.

mglobal-midas-fasanara.title: Receivables, With Rails
mglobal-midas-fasanara.text: mGLOBAL is Midas's tokenized certificate over Fasanara's global private-credit strategy, largely short-dated trade receivables and digital invoices from SMEs. It accrues NAV through issuer-priced portfolio performance, so the important sentence is the boring one: this is not a fixed $1 payment stablecoin. Pharos models the reserve as a single high-risk Fasanara strategy slice and surfaces the contract-priced strategy-token warning because secondary-market volume is not doing much work here. The Midas attestation engine provides daily NAV and proof tooling, but primary issuance and redemption remain permissioned through Midas rails. Utility improved in June when mGLOBAL went live as collateral on Aave's Horizon RWA market with tens of millions in TVL, giving the certificate its first serious borrowing venue. The appeal is access to an asset-backed lending portfolio; the bill comes as issuer discretion, private-credit opacity, and a 1-of-3 admin posture that does not scream institutional serenity.

mhyper-midas.title: Market Neutral, Maybe
mhyper-midas.text: mHYPER is a Midas tokenized debt instrument tracking Hyperithm-managed market-neutral stablecoin strategies across on-chain markets and institutional execution venues. The mechanism is daily NAV appreciation, not a fixed $1 peg, and tokenholders hold a subordinated claim against Midas rather than ownership of the underlying assets. Pharos can value it through the Midas attestation stack and Chainlink-verified NAV route, but the reserve is still one high-risk strategy sleeve held under Fordefi MPC custody with issuer-admin controls. Primary mint and redeem access is permissioned for greenlisted users, with instant exits relying on Midas Staked Liquidity rather than an unconditional cash floor. Market neutral is the strategy label; counterparty neutral is very much not the product.

mmev-midas.title: Strategy Wrapper, New Driver
mmev-midas.text: mMEV is a Midas NAV token whose original strategy manager no longer runs it: after the deUSD daisy-chain implosion gutted MEV Capital's assets, Midas concluded all business with the firm in February 2026 and handed strategy and risk oversight to RockawayX, processing pending redemptions at the last verified price. The wrapper survived its manager, which is either a compliment to the wrapper or a warning about strategy tokens generally. The token accrues through NAV appreciation and mints or redeems through Midas rails, not through an open par redemption path built for payments. Daily self-reported Midas transparency gives Pharos a valuation route, but the underlying strategy remains high-risk, complex, and not especially interested in being mistaken for a checking account. The Midas control stack adds its own concentrated-admin flavor, because apparently tokenized strategy access was not already operationally spicy enough.

mapollo-midas.title: Apollo Crypto Strategy via Midas
mapollo-midas.text: mAPOLLO is the Midas liquid-yield wrapper for an Apollo Crypto managed strategy, not the Apollo credit fund and not a transactional stablecoin. Its value follows NAV appreciation through permissioned Midas mint and redeem rails, while the reserve risk is high because the backing is digital-asset strategy exposure rather than cash or bills. Pharos keeps the self-reported Midas transparency and NAV route in view, but that does not make the underlying strategy any less manager-dependent. This is useful if you want tokenized strategy access; it is less charming if you were hoping the word Apollo would magically turn crypto yield into a bank deposit.

safo-spiko-usd.title: Spiko Smart Cash USD Share Class
safo-spiko-usd.text: SAFO is the USD share class of Spiko and Amundi's Smart Cash exposure, built around fully collateralized overnight total-return swaps rather than direct T-bill ownership. That distinction matters: Pharos classifies the reserve as medium-risk RWA strategy exposure because the holder is exposed to fund structure, swap counterparties, collateral packages, and regulated NAV mechanics. The AMF/UCITS context and PwC audit coverage help, but they do not turn a fund share into a simple par-redeemable stablecoin. Primary market access remains permissioned through Spiko rails, with subscriptions and redemptions happening at fund NAV. The franchise keeps scaling. Spiko pushed the fund natively onto Solana in early July, its first deployment beyond EVM and Stellar rails, with flows settling in Circle's stablecoins. SAFO is conservative by DeFi standards and still absolutely a fund share, which is exactly the nuance stablecoin tickers are built to blur.

spkcc-spiko.title: The Carry Trade Goes Regulated
spkcc-spiko.text: SPKCC is the dollar share class of Spiko's Digital Assets Cash & Carry Fund, a French professional-fund vehicle whose NAV comes from BTC and ETH {{term:basis-trade}}basis trades{{/term}} rotated against short-duration T-bills. It is a fund share wearing a stablecoin's ticker, not a dollar promise. The institutional plumbing is unusually complete for crypto carry: Marex as sole strategy counterparty, Coinbase for spot {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, CME for cleared futures, and CACEIS Bank as ACPR-licensed depositary striking a daily NAV. The card rises from D to C because the fund prospectus and a dated export of the AMF's own register of authorised management companies were read directly, establishing prudential supervision through the manager and a recurring, independently administered reconciliation. Two caveats must travel with that upgrade: the FPS itself is not AMF-authorised. The prudential hook is the AIFM, depositary, and distributor, not the vehicle. Reporting is annual, and the first financial year does not close until December 2026, so PwC's statutory opinion does not yet exist. Meanwhile the reserve side remains one unsplit strategy envelope; Pharos knows the fund is doing carry and knows nothing about the current spot, margin, or venue weights. Regulated sophistication is not the same thing as transparency, and here you are buying the former.

eursafo-spiko.title: EUR Smart Cash Through Spiko
eursafo-spiko.text: EURSAFO is the euro share class of Spiko and Amundi's Smart Cash fund, an AMF-authorized UCITS structure that behaves like a NAV-accreting fund token rather than a bank-deposit stablecoin. The reserve is fully collateralized overnight total-return swap exposure with tier-1 bank counterparties and liquid collateral, so Pharos treats it as medium-risk RWA strategy exposure instead of pretending it is a plain euro cash account. PwC quarterly audit coverage and regulated French fund status help, but subscriptions and redemptions still run through KYC-gated Spiko rails. Distribution is widening: Spiko opened Solana subscriptions and redemptions for the fund in early July, its first deployment beyond EVM and Stellar rails, settling through Circle's stablecoins. It is conservative by crypto standards and still absolutely a fund share, which is the sort of nuance stablecoin tickers tend to flatten on contact.

eurspkcc-spiko.title: Euro Carry, Fund First
eurspkcc-spiko.text: EURSPKCC is the euro share class of Spiko's Digital Assets Cash & Carry Fund, a French FPS alternative investment fund rather than a euro payment token: NAV accrues from fund performance and primary access is KYC-gated through Spiko's transfer rails, so read it as a fund share with euro accounting, not a one-euro promise. Its move from D to C mirrors the dollar class and rests on the same two artefacts: the fund prospectus naming CACEIS as daily administrator and depositary, and a dated AMF register export confirming the manager's portfolio-management authorisation. The euro side's own disclosure is much thinner. Its live share-class feed publishes a single undifferentiated cash-and-carry line with no constituent weights, its NAV travels through one administrative valuation path rather than a redundant feed, and an earlier evidence challenge found the product page's allocation data months out of date, which is why Pharos grades the reserve read here a notch below its dollar sibling. The assurance cadence is annual and still prospective: PwC is the appointed statutory auditor, but the first financial year does not close until December 2026, so the only recurring independent check is the depositary's daily NAV, not an audit opinion. Regulated packaging around crypto basis exposure is genuinely useful; it is not the same as being boring.

uktbl-spiko.title: Sterling T-Bills, Gated
uktbl-spiko.text: UKTBL is Spiko's GBP-denominated UK Treasury-bill money-market fund share, not a dollar product and not a retail payment stablecoin. The backing is pleasantly dull by crypto standards: mostly UK T-bills plus a small cash and bank-deposit buffer, audited by PwC under AMF UCITS short-term VNAV money-market fund rules. The tradeoff is access, because subscriptions, transfers, and redemptions are KYC-gated through Spiko fund rails at NAV rather than settled by permissionless on-chain arbitrage. Pharos treats the collateral as low-risk tokenized RWA exposure while keeping centralized issuer controls, blacklistability, and unresolved non-Ethereum mint surfaces visible. The reserves are boring in the best possible way; the operating model is fund administration with a token attached.

gbpsafo-spiko.title: GBP Smart Cash Share Class
gbpsafo-spiko.text: GBPSAFO is the GBP share of Spiko's UCITS Amundi Smart Cash {{term:money-market-fund}}MMF{{/term}}: a permissioned NAV share with overnight-swap exposure, not a retail GBP stablecoin. GBPSAFO extends Spiko Smart Cash coverage to a sterling-denominated share class. The reserve description follows the same fully collateralized overnight total-return swap structure as the USD and EUR SAFO classes, so the {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} risk model is medium rather than pure cash. The token is best understood as a permissioned NAV share, not a retail GBP stablecoin.

eur0-usual.title: Usual's Euro Treasury Wrapper
eur0-usual.text: EUR0 is Usual's euro stablecoin minted from tokenized Eurozone T-bill collateral such as Spiko's EUTBL; centralized issuer rails. EUR0 is Usual's euro-denominated stable asset, admitted through CoinGecko market data and an Ethereum contract. The reserve thesis points to Spiko's euTBL tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} exposure rather than a simple euro bank-deposit account, making EUR0 an {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-backed dependency token with centralized issuer rails. The supply is still small, but it gives the dashboard a useful euro reference from the Usual ecosystem. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} and backstop quality remain intentionally conservative until Usual-specific terms are reviewed. Spiko EUTBL is a tokenized {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market{{/term}}-style euro T-bill fund.

emxn-telcoin.title: Telcoin's Mexican Peso Cash Token
emxn-telcoin.text: eMXN is Telcoin's centralized MXN stablecoin on Polygon; reserves are issuer-reported with no public per-token feed yet. eMXN extends Telcoin's Digital Cash model from eUSD into Mexican peso settlement. CoinGecko supplies price and market-cap coverage, and the Polygon deployment gives Pharos a straightforward contract anchor. The issuer framing is bank-style payment infrastructure rather than a permissionless {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}, so reserve confidence depends on Telcoin's off-chain controls and reporting. No public per-token reserve feed is currently documented in the reviewed materials. {{term:custody}}Custody{{/term}} sits with the issuer and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through Telcoin's wallet rails.

hchf-hedera-swiss-franc.title: Hedera's Small CHF Experiment
hchf-hedera-swiss-franc.text: HCHF is a Swiss-franc synthetic minted against HBAR troves on Hedera, closer to Liquity wearing a CHF coat than to a regulated franc account. Borrowers create HCHF from overcollateralized HBAR positions, undercollateralized troves are liquidated through the Stability Pool, and face-value redemptions against collateral are the peg-defense mechanism. The upside is unusually clean on-chain control: the Hedera token has no admin, freeze, wipe, or pause key, and Pharos marks governance as immutable-code rather than issuer discretion. The downside is equally plain: collateral is volatile HBAR, liquidity is tiny, and anyone expecting the comfort of a Swiss bank attestation has wandered into the wrong canton.

eurot-token-teknoloji.title: Token Teknoloji's Euro Token
eurot-token-teknoloji.text: EUROT is Token Teknoloji's Turkish 1:1 euro stablecoin backed by bank reserves at Ziraat Participation and Akbank, without machine-readable {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. EUROT is Token Teknoloji's euro-backed reserve token with Avalanche and Polygon contract coverage through CoinGecko. The issuer describes a 1:1 euro reserve model and publishes official token materials, but the reviewed materials do not provide a machine-readable reserve or attestation feed. That makes EUROT useful for long-tail euro coverage while keeping reserve confidence and {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} transparency below larger MiCA-era issuers with recurring attestations.

mxne-real-mxn.title: Brale and Etherfuse's MXN Rail
mxne-real-mxn.text: Brale + Etherfuse MXN peso payment token on Base, Solana, and Stellar with issuer redemption; Base proxy-owner control flagged by CoinGecko and no public live reserve feed. MXNe is a Mexican peso token associated with Brale and Etherfuse, with CoinGecko price coverage and deployments on Base, Solana, and Stellar. The public description points to 1:1 MXN backing under regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, so the model is closer to a fiat-reserve payment token than a crypto CDP. The main caveat is control risk: the Base contract has proxy-owner concerns in CoinGecko's token-risk metadata, and no live reserve feed or independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} cadence is currently public.

wmxn-ripio.title: Ripio's Missing MXN Wrapper
wmxn-ripio.text: wMXN completes Ripio's wFIAT set with a Mexican peso asset across the same EVM footprint as the rest of the suite, with reserve transparency the recurring weak point. wMXN completes the tracked Ripio wFIAT set with a Mexican peso asset deployed across the same EVM footprint as WBRL, WCLP, WCOP, and WPEN. DefiLlama provides the live price and circulating-supply path, while Ripio's official local-stablecoin page describes 1:1 local-currency {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} backing and on/off-ramp {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} via {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} infrastructure. As with the rest of the Ripio suite, the weak point is reserve transparency: public materials describe the backing model but do not expose a reliable per-token attestation feed.

jpyt-dephaser.title: A High-Risk Yen Synthetic
jpyt-dephaser.text: Algorithmic yen on Base/Optimism minted against locked USDT/USDC using an FX oracle; thin liquidity, high-dependency collateral. JPYT is Dephaser's yen-pegged token on Base and Optimism. CoinGecko describes the design as an algorithmic JPY stablecoin backed by locked USDT, making the reserve view high-risk dependency collateral rather than a cash yen reserve. Price and market-cap coverage are present, but the supply is small and the peg depends on Dephaser's mechanism, USDT collateral quality, and thin secondary liquidity. The mechanism is closer to {{term:algorithmic}}algorithmic{{/term}} FX synthesis than fiat backing, with {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} returning the locked USDT or USDC collateral rather than yen cash.

euro3-3a-dao.title: A Tiny Overcollateralized Euro CDP
euro3-3a-dao.text: EURO3 is 3A DAO's overcollateralized euro {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin on Polygon and Linea, minted against crypto collateral in user-owned vaults. EURO3 is a 3A DAO euro stablecoin created through {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} vault borrowing and burned when users repay or redeem against collateral. DefiLlama supplies price and circulating-balance data, with current activity split across Linea and Polygon, but there is no CoinGecko geckoId and supply is very small. The design gives Pharos a crypto-backed euro reference, while liquidity, oracle depth, and governance details remain the practical risk areas.

krwo-gimswap.title: GimSwap's KRW Voucher Token
krwo-gimswap.text: KRW-pegged stablecoin issued against Open Voucher KRW vouchers at 10,000:1 on Kaia and BNB Chain; CoinGecko flags unrestricted minting risk on BSC. KRWO is a Korean-won stable asset linked to GimSwap and Open Voucher, with CoinGecko coverage on Kaia and BNB Chain. Available materials point to KRW-backed issuance, but reserve and redemption evidence is still thinner than for regulated fiat issuers. CoinGecko's token-risk metadata flags unrestricted minting risk on BNB Chain, keeping the control profile conservative until admin permissions and dilution controls are clearer. The voucher-based issuance lacks third-party {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} and transparent {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, leaving the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path entirely dependent on GimSwap's own voucher infrastructure.

xofm-mento.title: Mento's CFA Franc CDP
xofm-mento.text:
Mento's West African CFA franc CDP mints XOFm against USDm collateral on Celo, with FX-pair modeling still maturing on the reserve side.

XOFm brings Mento's local-currency {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} model to the West African CFA franc on Celo. DefiLlama shows a live price and circulating supply, and the protocol description is clear: users deposit USDm into Mento troves and borrow XOFm against it, with {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} buffers and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} mechanics enforcing peg discipline. Pharos now treats XOF as a dedicated peg with a secondary daily FX reference, while reserve modeling stays conservative because Mento's live CDP data does not expose XOFm-specific trove rows yet.

xnk-kinka.title: Japanese Gold Bullion Token
xnk-kinka.text:
Kinka tokenizes one troy ounce of 99.99% Japanese gold per XNK, with Cardano- and Ethereum-issued supply against centralized issuer custody.

XNK represents one fine troy ounce equivalent of 99.99% Japanese-brand physical gold bullion held through Kinka's issuer and storage arrangements. The Cardano deployment is recorded alongside Ethereum, and the reserve model treats the backing as physical gold with centralized custody and issuer-controlled exchange terms. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} into physical bars is possible only through the documented KYC process and size thresholds, with no public per-token {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} cadence yet integrated.

gynusd-gyndore.title: The cbBTC-Only CDP
gynusd-gyndore.text: gynUSD is a pre-launch CDP stablecoin built around a single, blunt proposition: cbBTC is the only collateral. By focusing exclusively on Bitcoin through Coinbase's wrapper, Gyndore sidesteps the generalized risk models that force multi-asset lending markets into conservative LTV ratios. It then passes the capital efficiency benefit directly to borrowers, with a 110% minimum collateralization ratio enabling up to 90.91% LTV. Seventy percent of borrow fees flow to Stability Pool depositors, removing the idle-liquidity drag that burdens pool-based lending markets. The governance story has two possible endings depending on launch conditions: the protocol can either start with a bootstrapping admin key and transition to GYND token governance once the fee switch triggers, or mint GYND from day one if pre-launch capital formation is sufficient. The Pareto Controller constrains GYND voters to ±10bps rate adjustments and requires 80% consensus. This governance behaves more like a thermostat than a parliament. The cbBTC dependency is the structural asterisk: Coinbase custody sits at the base of every loan, so the trust-minimized pitch has a ceiling.

tgld-tenbin.title: Synthetic Gold, Not Bullion
tgld-tenbin.text: tGLD is Tenbin's tokenized gold note, but unlike PAXG or XAUT it holds no vaulted metal. Each token is a Tenbin AssetCo (BVI) debt-note representing the U.S.-dollar value of one troy ounce of gold, collateralized by USDC and hedged with CME gold futures rather than allocated bullion. Mint and redemption are KYC-gated through a Controller and a backend signer that holds the on-chain minter role, and redemptions settle in a USD stablecoin instead of physical metal. Launched on Ethereum mainnet in February 2026 after a $7M Galaxy Ventures-led seed and four security audits, it remains in private beta, roughly $0.3M outstanding across about 36 holders, with its only public market a near-dormant Uniswap V4 pool and no independent proof-of-reserves attestation. Pharos lists tGLD as pre-launch until its public price feed updates frequently enough to clear the gold pricing-freshness gate; a staked yield variant (stGLD) and testnet FX siblings (tBRL, tMXN) round out Tenbin's roadmap.

ejpy-jbfd.title: The Trust-Bank Yen That Skips the Cap
ejpy-jbfd.text: EJPY is Japan Blockchain Foundation's pre-launch yen stablecoin, and its whole pitch is a legal classification: a trust-type Type III electronic payment instrument that escapes the ¥1M-per-transaction ceiling JPYC has spent years working around. JBFD, the consortium operator behind Japan Open Chain, would be the settlor, with reserves parked in a licensed trust bank that, as of the May 2026 announcement, it is still negotiating with and has not named. That gap is the tell: trust-segregated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and statutory {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rights are the entire value proposition, yet the trustee, the reserve mix, and the launch date are all blank. The plan is to issue on Japan Open Chain first and Ethereum next, sometime within fiscal 2026 (which runs through March 2027), aimed squarely at B2B settlement rather than retail DeFi. EJPY is a credible institutional play in a market suddenly crowded with yen-stablecoin contenders. JPYSC, JPYC, and a megabank consortium all circle the same FSA framework. Right now, this is a decision to issue, not a token you can hold.

aed-rakbank.title: The First Commercial-Bank Dirham
aed-rakbank.text: AED-RAKBANK is RAKBank's pre-launch dirham stablecoin, notable less for what it is than for who is issuing it: the first conventional commercial bank to win CBUAE in-principle approval for an AED payment token, as opposed to the digital-bank and sovereign-wealth vehicles (Zand AED, AE Coin, the FAB/ADQ/IHC effort) that got there first. The January 2026 nod arrives under the UAE's Payment Token Services Regulation, which permits payment use only for dirham-backed tokens and demands a published white paper plus full reserves. RAKBank's plan ticks the regulatory boxes: it calls for 1:1 dirhams in segregated regulated accounts, full par {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, audited contracts, and real-time reserve {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. However, 'in-principle' is doing heavy lifting: no ticker, no chain, no issuing subsidiary, and no launch date have been disclosed, and the regulation may force RAKBank into a separate licensed issuer it hasn't confirmed. Pharos tracks the AED peg as OTHER until dirham support is built. A pilot is promised 'in due course,' which in regulatory dialect means watch this space.

bils-bitsofgold.title: Israel's First Regulated Shekel
bils-bitsofgold.text: BILS is the first shekel stablecoin to clear an Israeli regulator, and unlike most entries on this list it is approved rather than merely announced; Bits of Gold spent two years in a sandbox before the Capital Market, Insurance and Savings Authority signed off in April 2026. The conditions are unusually concrete for a pre-launch asset: 1:1 New Israeli Shekel backing held in segregated bank accounts inside Israel (foreign custody explicitly barred), an Ernst & Young audit, Fireblocks issuance infrastructure, and QEDIT zero-knowledge privacy, all on Solana via token extensions. Reach is limited: the regulator is requiring a deliberately gradual, small-scale rollout, likely to institutions first, with no firm public-launch date and no DefiLlama or CoinGecko footprint yet. That throttled debut, plus a peg Pharos doesn't yet price (tracked as OTHER until shekel support lands), is exactly why it sits in pre-launch rather than the live table. Note the regulatory lane: this is a CMISA rulebook approval, not the broader Israeli Stablecoin Law, which is still stuck in draft. A real, audited, regulator-blessed shekel, just not one you can buy in size yet.

autousd-auto-finance.title: An Autopool Dollar Wrapper
autousd-auto-finance.text: autoUSD is Auto Finance's USDC autopool share token on Ethereum: holders own a vault receipt rather than a fiat-reserve stablecoin, and the share price is expected to rise as strategy earnings auto-compound. The protocol documentation describes autopools that rebalance across eligible DeFi destinations in search of stronger risk-adjusted returns, so the dollar anchor comes from USDC as the vault asset while the extra risk comes from destination selection, liquidity, and controller operations. Pharos tracks the Ethereum autoUSD contract directly, with market-cap coverage from on-chain supply and price coverage from the contract quote path, while Royco Dawn adds the senior/junior tranche market that motivated this listing. The result is useful yield coverage, but the reserve model stays conservative: this is a strategy wrapper over USDC, not a redeemable issuer dollar.

eearn-ember.title: Ember's Royco-Listed Vault Share
eearn-ember.text: eEARN is Ember's yield-bearing USDC vault share tracked on Ethereum for Royco Dawn coverage. The token behaves like a NAV wrapper: deposits mint vault shares, withdrawals return the vault asset, and market value should follow the USDC-denominated share price rather than a flat issuer redemption claim. CoinGecko currently exposes the Ember Earn market through its Sui-side row, so Pharos uses that as a price source while forcing market cap through the Ethereum token's on-chain supply to avoid mixing chains. Royco Dawn then wraps the same eEARN deposit token into senior and junior tranche vaults, which is valuable yield context but also why the reserve and governance posture stay high-risk and wrapper-focused.

dusd-dialectic.title: Dialectic's Book, Tokenised
dusd-dialectic.text:
DUSD is a USDC-accounted Makina strategy share, not a fixed-dollar claim: its price follows Dialectic's marked AUM per share. The portfolio rotates through DeFi venues under an approved instruction set, and Pharos can read first-party live accounting for its allocations, debt, supply, and NAV.

The exit route now has a live same-block capacity bound, calculated as idle Ethereum USDC minus the liability of DUSD already locked in the queue. That backlog-adjusted number is a conditional liquidity proxy, not a reserved buffer or funding promise. The reviewed contract processes request IDs sequentially and currently charges no redemption fee, while the Machine Terms grant neither a contractual redemption right nor queue priority; finalization has no maximum SLA, requests may remain unfilled indefinitely, and the operator may cease the Machine without notice. Custody is equally blunt: Dialectic owns deposited and deployed assets outright, holders receive no trust, proprietary, priority, or bankruptcy-remote claim, and the optional Security Module carries no contractual backstop obligation. DUSD itself has no reviewed local freeze path, but upstream USDC can still be frozen; Recovery Mode cannot move Circle-frozen funds, and wallet or request-NFT transfers remain subject to verification and discretionary fill, leaving thin DEX liquidity and the issuer queue as two versions of the same exit problem.

ousd-open-standard.title: The Everything-Consortium Dollar
ousd-open-standard.text: Open USD is what happens when 140-plus of the biggest names in payments and banking, including Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Stripe, BlackRock, BNY Mellon, and Coinbase, decide they would rather split reserve income among themselves than hand it to Circle. Announced June 30, 2026 and operated by an independent company, Open Standard, whose board is drawn from its own partners, OUSD promises fee-free minting, no volume limits, and most of the reserve yield routed back to the businesses that adopt it. The pitch is GENIUS Act compliance and neutral, shared governance; the reality, still, is a launch announcement with no mainnet contracts, named custodian, or attestation. Markets took it seriously anyway. Circle's stock fell roughly 15-17% on the news, even though some OUSD backers such as BlackRock and BNY are also core partners in Circle's own ecosystem. The unresolved question is the one that has dogged every mega-consortium before it: 140 partners are easy to announce and very hard to align. Launch is promised 'later in 2026,' natively on Solana with a broader rollout to Polygon, Stellar, and Aptos to follow. As of mid-August, the token still isn't live.

rd-rai-dollar.title: RAI, Finally Pinned to a Dollar
rd-rai-dollar.text: RAI proved a stablecoin could be steered by an on-chain controller rather than a committee, and the market followed the redemption price faithfully; that price was not a dollar, and most of the market could not get past it. RAI Dollar keeps the machinery and pins the target. RD is an immutable CDP stablecoin on Ethereum where a PI controller reads a 24-hour TWAP of the market price and moves one system-wide borrow rate, bounded to 0.25-50% APY around a 2% bias, until supply and demand pull the price back to $1, with Liquity's redemption arbitrage as the floor. The par lever RAI made famous survives, bounded to $0.75-$1.30 and moving no faster than a tenth of a cent an hour, held for the extremes rather than left to float. Collateral sits in eight isolated branches: WETH, wstETH, rETH, weETH, WBTC, tBTC, sUSDS, and PAXG, each with its own troves, stability pool, and shutdown path. The question Liquity V2 left open is answered by routing a slice of healthy-branch fees to repair an undercollateralized branch rather than convening a vote. Borrowers who dislike the redemption queue can pay a floating Redemption Shield surcharge that funds a matching discount for everyone who does not. All of it is still theoretical: no contracts are deployed, the address registry reads TBD, the core repository is private, and the audits, part-funded by an August 2026 Ethereum Foundation subsidy, are still in progress. Immutability cuts both ways, and whatever ships is what runs, permanently.

sources.label: RAI Dollar docs: How it stays stable

eurr-revolut.title: The Neobank That Rented Its Own Coin
eurr-revolut.text: EURR is live, and Pharos tracks it pre-launch anyway. Revolut launched it on August 26 2026 as the first product of a stablecoin programme long assumed to be arriving in dollars or sterling, phased into Denmark, Poland, and Portugal with the rest of the EEA promised later in the year. The structural surprise is the issuer: not Revolut's Lithuanian EMI, which had every licence required, but Bridge Building S.A., the Luxembourg arm of Stripe-owned Bridge, holding an EMI licence and MiCA authorisation from the CSSF while Revolut Digital Assets Europe distributes under its CySEC permission. Europe's biggest neobank built the distribution and outsourced the balance sheet: the same Bridge Open Issuance model behind MoneyGram's and Deel's tokens, now wearing a consumer brand with 80 million customers behind it. The timing is not subtle either: EURR arrived as Revolut finished pulling Tether's USDt from European retail on August 31, so the euro rail it removed and the euro rail it added are the same shelf. Supply went from 366 to roughly 251,000 tokens in two days, which is a rollout, not yet adoption. MiCA does not force reserve composition, custodians, or {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} cadence into public view; all remain undisclosed, and no accepted price source resolves the token, which is precisely why it sits here rather than in the tracked set. A stablecoin distributed by a bank, issued by a payments company, and priced by nobody is a fair snapshot of where regulated euro tokens currently are.
